title: The emitted opener builds a verified TLS configuration
when: Builds a database configuration with sslmode verify-full.
then: Expects a TLS configuration that verifies the server and requires TLS 1.2 or later.

title: The emitted opener takes no password, trust, client certificate or service from the files under HOME
when: HOME names a folder with a .pgpass that gives each database a password, a .pg_service.conf with a service home, and a root certificate, a client certificate and a client key under .postgresql. Builds a database configuration with sslmode verify-full from a keyword/value string and from URLs: with a user, with the user in the query, with a password that holds a '?', and with two hosts and a closing '&'; then from a string that names the service home; then from strings that name a root certificate file of their own.
then: Expects each configuration to have no password from the pass file, no root certificate pool, no client certificate and the host of the string; the service to be refused; and the root certificate that a string names to be kept.
notes: Follow-up of the security review of PR #353, L2: pgx reads HOME for its default pass file, service file and certificate files when the connection string does not give them. The opener gives each of them first, empty, so a setting of DATABASE_URL comes later and wins. The release scan holds postgres-adapter and postgres-client to declare HOME (ST-SUP-UC01-R10-T01). Mutations caught (agents/followups/fu-92/mut-home.py, 9 of 9).

title: Concurrent migration jobs apply each migration once and in name order
given: A schema-generation database that the migration job bootstrapped, on PostgreSQL whose collation is en_US, and three new function migrations registered out of their name order: 980_x_z and 980_xy, which insert their name into a table, and 950_ledger_runs, which makes that table. The names 980_x_z and 980_xy sort in one order by bytes and in the other order by the en_US collation.
when: Runs Migrate four times at the same time on the database, reads the table and the ledger, and runs Migrate again.
then: Expects each run to pass, the table to hold 950_ledger_runs, 980_x_z and 980_xy once each and in that order, the ledger to end with the same three versions in that order, and the last run to apply nothing.
notes: Level: integration, against PostgreSQL from pgtest, through the generated module of TestGeneratedSchemaGeneration. Proved by TestMigrationLedgerAppliesOnceInOrder, subtest ST-SUP-RC01-OC11-T05. The ledger runs on database/sql: each pending migration and its ledger row commit in one transaction that takes the ledger lock and reads the ledger again, and the ledger reads in the byte order of the version (COLLATE "C"). Mutations caught: applyPending without the ledger lock (a run fails when two runs apply one migration), orderedMigrations without its sort (980_x_z runs before its table), and the ledger read without COLLATE "C" (the next run refuses its own ledger).

title: Concurrent migration jobs apply each migration once under a default isolation of repeatable read
given: A schema-generation database that the migration job bootstrapped, set with ALTER DATABASE to default_transaction_isolation repeatable read, a new pool whose connections start with that setting, and two new function migrations: 990_rr_runs, which makes a table and inserts its name, and 991_rr_next, which inserts its name.
when: Runs Migrate eight times at the same time, each on its own connection of the new pool, and reads the table.
then: Expects each run to pass, and the table to hold 990_rr_runs and 991_rr_next once each and in that order.
notes: Level: integration, against PostgreSQL from pgtest, through the generated module of TestGeneratedSchemaGeneration. Proved by TestMigrationLedgerIgnoresDefaultIsolation, subtest ST-SUP-RC01-OC11-T06. applyPending and ApplyMigration open their ledger transactions at read committed, so each statement takes its snapshot after the ledger lock is granted. Finding L1 of the security review of PR 217. Mutation caught: applyPending with the default isolation of the database (a waiting job reads the ledger of its earlier snapshot and applies a migration again). The concurrent use of ApplyMigration has no test of its own.

title: An external apply that runs at once with migration jobs applies its body once, and only after the registered history
given: A schema-generation database that the migration job bootstrapped, set with ALTER DATABASE to default_transaction_isolation repeatable read, a new pool whose connections start with that setting, and a new function migration 996_apply_pending that makes a table of runs and inserts its name, whose first run holds the ledger lock until the test releases it.
when: Runs an external apply (ApplyMigration) of 997_apply_external, which inserts its name, while 996_apply_pending is pending. Then starts four migration jobs, waits until one runs 996_apply_pending, starts four external applies of 997_apply_external, waits until the three other jobs and the four applies all wait on the ledger lock, and releases it. Then, on a fresh database with the same setting that a migration job bootstrapped, runs eight external applies of 998_apply_again, which waits 0.2 s and inserts its name, at the same moment.
then: Expects the first apply refused with the ledger error; each job and apply after it to pass or to be refused with the ledger error only; exactly one apply of 997_apply_external to pass, one ledger row of it, and the runs to be 996_apply_pending once and then the external body once, with the pending migration just before it in the ledger. Expects exactly one of the eight applies of 998_apply_again to pass and its body to run once.
notes: Level: integration, against PostgreSQL from pgtest, through the generated storage package, which TestGeneratedSchemaGeneration builds and runs with go test -race; the server is the one that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names, a local postgres:17.7 container without privilege (ST-STD-LOCAL). Follow-up of PR #217 (missing test: concurrent ApplyMigration against Migrate) and its recheck (ApplyMigration has the READ COMMITTED fix but no concurrent test). Mutation caught in four of four runs: ApplyMigration at the default isolation of the database (a duplicate ledger key). The #231 review found that the first phase passed with no external apply; it now holds the pending migration open, so every apply meets it, and requires one pass. Mutations caught: ApplyMigration at the default isolation (no apply passed); no refusal of a pending registered history (the first apply ran its body).

title: A fill that holds the budget and an insert that does not lock it do not deadlock, and the sum sees the committed row
given: The Allocation declaration of ST-SUP-RC01-OC19-T01 with a command add-allocation that writes Budget and Allocation and whose fill calls GetForUpdate on the budget, and a command create-allocation that writes Allocation and takes no parent lock, generated into a temporary folder, and a real PostgreSQL 16 server.
when: With Retry on conflict 0: T1 runs add-allocation on budget b1, whose fill calls GetForUpdate on b1 and waits at a barrier; T2 runs create-allocation, which inserts an Allocation of b1 and commits, so that its foreign key check takes FOR KEY SHARE on b1 and its trigger waits for T1, and the test waits until pg_locks shows T2 waiting for T1; then T1 inserts an Allocation of b1 and commits. First with amounts that both fit the limit, then with amounts that fit only one at a time.
then: Expects no 40P01 in either case. Expects both to commit in the first case. In the second case expects T1 to commit and T2 to be refused by the trigger, so the sum that T2's trigger reads holds T1's committed row; a trigger that reads the sum in the statement that takes the lock keeps its old snapshot and lets T2 commit, and fails this case.
notes: Level: integration. Not automated yet: the generator does not emit invariants or commands yet. Planned file internal/generator/postgresadapter/testdata/sum_limit_test.go. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at a pinned image digest. Review of PR #130: a FOR UPDATE in the trigger deadlocked with a parent locked by GetForUpdate. Review of 97214683: the earlier sequence passed with the old trigger too, because both fills locked the parent first.

Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it.

title: The generated migration job runs as the owner role and the service as the runtime role
given: The rest-crud service wiring-shop of internal/compiler/testdata/runtime_wiring/project/service.yaml with pooled tenancy, spicedb-authz, audit-log and idempotency on the runtime data path: the collection orders over the owned entity Order (sku, qty) with create, read, list, patch and delete, the command add-note that writes a Note of an order on the permission edit, and the query get-order-summary that reads an Order on the permission view, each with its fill; generated with stego apply from a project with no record, built, and run against PostgreSQL and SpiceDB, with the roles and grants that the role migration of the tenancy component makes (ST-SUP-RC27-OC04).
when: Runs the migration job with the login of the owner role, starts the service with a login of the runtime role, and reads the owners of the tables of public and the roles of the connections of the server.
then: Expects the tables orders, notes and idempotency_keys made, every table of public owned by the owner role, no relation owned by the runtime role, every connection of the service as the runtime role, and no connection as the login of the migration job.
notes: Level: system. internal/compiler/runtime_wiring_test.go (TestRuntimeWiring) builds the stego binary of the commit, runs stego apply in a project with internal/compiler/testdata/runtime_wiring/project and a copy of the registry whose rest-crud archetype holds the command, query, tenancy, domain-probe and outbox components, builds the generated service with the pinned Go (STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO) against the runtime module of this repository, and runs the check of this file once in the generated module: it runs the binary with the argument migrate as the migration job and then the binary as the service, and calls it over HTTP. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, with TLS that the check turns on with a certificate of its own CA, and a local SpiceDB serve container of the pinned image authzed/spicedb:v1.57.0 with a memory datastore, without privilege, which the test starts and removes; a missing server fails the test. The login of the migration job is the owner role, as the outbox migration needs (ST-SUP-RP01-LC19); the role migration of the tenancy component makes that login a member of the outbox relay role of the service WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE (ST-SUP-RC27-OC04), as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 and the orchestrator in ST-SUP-Q106. The migration job sets the owner role in each step on one connection. Mutation caught: the steps of the migration job as the runtime role. A step as the login role is not seen, because the login is the owner role. The service runs all modes: its worker mode connects as the worker role and its relay as the relay role (ST-SUP-RP14-LC04), so the check accepts these two roles beside the runtime role, and ST-SUP-RC01-OC41-T04 checks TLS on the connections of all three.

title: The start check refuses a runtime role that is the owner role or a member of it
given: The database of ST-SUP-RP14-LC02-T01, migrated as the owner role, and a connection as its runtime role.
when: Runs the start check of New with the parts of the service; then with the parts whose owner role is the runtime role; then once with each membership of the owner role granted to the runtime role and revoked after: with no inherit and no set, with inherit, and through a role between them; then with the parts of the service again.
then: Expects the first and the last checks to give no error, and each other check to be refused with a message that the runtime role is the owner role or a member of it.
notes: Level: integration. Follow-up of the security review of PR #348 (low): the generator refused a runtime role that is the owner role (ST-SUP-RC01-OC32-T02), and the comment and the test notes said that the start check refused it too, which was not so. The owner role owns the tables, so their row-level security does not hold it, and the sync trigger passes the writes of a transaction that names the change in stego.backfill_change. A role is a member of itself and a superuser of each role, so pg_has_role MEMBER covers all three. Mutations caught (agents/followups/fu-93/mut.py, 4 of 4): the role itself not counted; no membership read; only a membership with inherit counted; no refusal.

title: Each schema step gives one migration in order, from the declaration alone

title: Each add step gives one migration after the baseline, in order, from the declaration alone
when: Generates a pooled service whose Board has a title, with three add steps: the owned entity Card that refers to a Board and has an optional unique code, the optional field Board.note with a minimum and a maximum length that a list searches, and the field Board.rank with a default; generates it twice, and generates the release before the steps, and a service whose baseline holds Card, with their tenancy components. Then generates the service with a rename step, a contract step of an add, a required field with no default, a reference to an entity that a later step adds, and a change with no step.
then: Expects migrate.go to register 001_initial, 100_tenancy_row_security and step_0001_add-card_expand, step_0002_add-board-note_expand, its _index_01 and its _validate, step_0003_add-board-rank_expand and its _index_01 in that order, a step with RegisterStep, an index build with RegisterIndexStep and the name of its index, and a validation with RegisterValidateStep; the names to sort in that order, and the ledger name check to accept the names of an index build and of a validation and to refuse _index_1 and _valid; 001_initial and the tenancy row-level security to be those of the release before; the Card step to be byte for byte the CREATE TABLE of cards and the row-level security of cards of the service whose baseline holds Card; each field step to add only its column and its CHECK NOT VALID, each index migration to be one CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS, and the validation to be one VALIDATE CONSTRAINT for each CHECK; the same bytes in each file of both runs; and each refused declaration to give no file and an error that names its cause.

title: An add step takes a database with rows to the schema of a new database, and the release before still runs on it
when: Runs the migration job of the Board release before the steps of ST-SUP-RC01-OC22-T02 on a new database as the owner role, writes a board as the runtime role, runs the migration job of the release with the three add steps, and reads the board, the ledger and the catalog; runs the ledger check, the schema generation check and the schema manifest check of the release before and the manifest check of the release with the steps; writes a board of the release before, cards of two tenants and a card of one tenant that refers to a board of another; reads the row-level security, the policies and the grants of cards and boards; runs the migration job of the release before again; runs the migration job of the release with the steps on a second new database; and, on a third new database, runs the migration job of the release before and then that of a release with only the adds that give no default (the table Card, the optional field Board.note, the optional reference Board.parent_id, whose foreign key the release before accepts in its exact form, ST-SUP-RP15-LC03, and the optional fields Board.level with integer bounds, Board.score with float bounds and Board.mood with the values of an enum, whose CHECK constraints and that of Board.note the release before accepts in their exact forms, ST-SUP-RP15-LC01), reads the CHECK constraints of boards, and runs the ledger, schema generation and schema manifest checks of both releases.
then: Expects the board of the release before to keep its title with no note and rank 0; the ledger to hold 001_initial and 100_tenancy_row_security with no compatible_with set and each step row, and each row of an index build and of a validation, with an empty set (ST-SUP-RC01-OC27); each check of both releases to accept the database, the schema manifest of the release before included, which accepts the constant default of the column rank that the add of Board.rank gives (ST-GEN-Q15 (a)); the release before to write a board; a card of one tenant not to be changed by another, a card into another tenant to be refused with 42501, and a card that refers to a board of another tenant to be refused with 23503; cards to have the row-level security, forced, the policy text and the grants of boards; the second run of the old migration job to change nothing; the catalogs of the two databases to be equal (ST-GEN-INV35); and, after the adds that give no default, boards to hold the CHECK constraints of level, mood, note and score, and each check of both releases to accept the database.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest ST-SUP-RC01-OC22-T03 of TestTables, which runs testdata/tables_test.go in the generated module. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN; without it the database part is skipped, and STEGO_REQUIRE_POSTGRES=1 makes that a failure.

title: A step waits for a lock only within its lock timeout and runs again, and a reader keeps getting its row
when: Runs the migration job of the Board release before the steps of ST-SUP-RC01-OC22-T02 and writes a board. A session holds an ACCESS SHARE lock on boards in an open transaction while the migration job of the release with the three add steps runs; when the step waits for its ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, a reader reads the board three times, each under a statement_timeout of 2.5 s, and the test checks the job after 2 s; then the session ends.
then: Expects each read to give the board, so no read waits for the holder behind the step; the job not to end while the session holds its lock, so it runs the step again after each lock timeout; and the job to end with no error after the session ends, with six step rows in the ledger (the probe of finding F1).
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest ST-SUP-RC01-OC22-T04 of TestTables. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN; the generated module of TestTables runs it.

title: An add step on a table with rows scans no row under its strong lock, and the release before restarts after each phase

Then applies, as the owner role and in ledger order, each migration of the release with only the adds that give no default of ST-SUP-RC01-OC22-T03 from its SQL file: each step in one transaction, reading pg_stat_xact_user_tables and pg_locks of boards before and after its body and pg_constraint of the constraints it adds; each index build outside a transaction; and each validation. After each migration it runs the schema generation check and the schema manifest check of the release before; at the end it reads the constraints of boards and runs the manifest check of the release with the steps.
then: Expects no scan of boards in the transaction of a step while it holds its ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, no index of boards built in it, each CHECK and foreign key it adds not yet validated, each index migration to be one CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS, the migrations of each phase to be there, both checks of the release before to accept the database after each migration, and at the end each constraint validated and the manifest of the release with the steps to accept the database (the probe of finding F2).
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest ST-SUP-RC01-OC22-T05 of TestTables. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN; the generated module of TestTables runs it.

title: The check reads the step tables on the search path pg_catalog, pg_temp, so an operator in public does not run in its compares
when: Migrates the rename of Board.title at expand with 100 rows and completes its backfill; adds a row of stego_schema.releases of the release before that reported a day ago; makes in public a function that raises and an operator * of integer and interval that runs it, a closer match than the one of pg_catalog (double precision) for the window of the release reports; computes 2 * interval '1 millisecond' on the search path of the session; then the contract step migrates on a session with the default search path.
then: Expects the compute on the search path of the session to raise the error of the operator in public, so the trap holds; and the contract step to finish (no old column, trigger, sync function or CHECK of the change left, and its ledger row written), so no compare of the check after the trigger read ran on the search path of the session.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestTables in the generated module. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN. Security review of PR #332, INFO-3: after the trigger read, the check set the search path back, so its reads of the backfills row, of pg_constraint, of the release reports and the count of rows left ran on the search path of the session. It now keeps pg_catalog, pg_temp up to its last read, and sets the path back only when it passes; a refusal or an error rolls the transaction back. Mutation caught (agents/followups/fu-91/mut.py): the path set back right after the trigger read.

title: The checkpoint row is the owner's and changes only by the fenced statement
when: Migrates a rename at expand; as the runtime role runs a plain UPDATE, a DELETE and an INSERT on stego_schema.backfills, backfill_read and the fenced checkpoint statement; as the owner role makes the lease row stego.backfill.board-title-rename of the holder job-a with the token 7, and runs the fenced checkpoint statement with the token 7 and with the stale token 3.
then: Expects the row to exist with its columns, owned by the owner role; each statement of the runtime role to be refused with SQLSTATE 42501; the two checkpoint functions to be SECURITY DEFINER with only search_path=pg_catalog, pg_temp, and neither PUBLIC nor the runtime role to have EXECUTE on either; and the fenced statement of the owner to change the row with the token 7 and to change nothing with the token 3.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest ST-SUP-RC01-OC25-T01 of TestTables in the generated module. The fenced checkpoint statement is the SECURITY DEFINER function stego_schema.backfill_checkpoint of the owner role, which the migration grants to no role (decision on finding M1 of the security review of PR #291, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14). It runs on PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN (ST-STD-LOCAL).

title: The runtime role cannot forge, poison or lock the backfill checkpoint
when: Applies the migration text of the backfill functions (registry/runtime/lease.BackfillFunctions, which the generator copies) as the owner role on a table of a rename at expand with 24 rows to move; gives the runtime role USAGE on stego_schema and SELECT and UPDATE on public.leases, as the migration job does; as the runtime role sets the lease row of the change to its own holder, then calls backfill_checkpoint to mark the change complete, calls it with the token 9223372036854775807, calls backfill_read for a FOR UPDATE lock of the row, and reads and changes stego_schema.backfills directly; then expires the lease and runs the backfill step of the job.
then: Expects both functions to be SECURITY DEFINER of the owner role with only search_path=pg_catalog, pg_temp and EXECUTE for the owner role alone, and PUBLIC to have no EXECUTE; each call of the runtime role to be refused with SQLSTATE 42501; the checkpoint row to keep the token 0 and not be complete; and the job then to move all 24 rows.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest ST-SUP-RC01-OC25-T02 of TestBackfillFunctions. It holds the attacks of finding M1 of the security review of PR #291 (decision on finding M1 of the security review of PR #291, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14). Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN.

title: An index build waits for an older transaction with no lock timeout, and is built once

Another session opens a REPEATABLE READ transaction that holds a snapshot and no lock on boards. Runs the migration job of the release with the step while that transaction stays open for 3 s, longer than the lock timeout of 1 s of a step, then ends the transaction.

Runs the migration job of the release with the step when the trigger refuses two drops, and, on a new database, when it refuses each drop.
then: Expects each job to fail on the unique build, with no ledger row of the build. With two refused drops, the third drop to remove the invalid index and the error to name only the build failure. With each drop refused, the invalid index to stay after exactly 5 drops and the error to name it: the failed build left the invalid index public."boards_slug_key", and 5 drops of it failed (finding L-B of the final security review of PR #270).
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest ST-SUP-RC01-OC38-T04 of TestTables. Mutations: mutations/b8.py in the notes of the builder. The trigger counts with no sequence: after a checkpoint nextval gives the transaction of the drop an ID, and DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY then fails as it is not the first action of its transaction, so a drop runs once more (the flake of run 43577566794; proved with a CHECKPOINT before each drop, fu-64/proof.py in the notes of the follow-up worker). #303 info: the count of drops is asserted, so a loop that drops fewer times than its message says fails (mutation: 4 drops, caught).

title: A contract waits for locks only within its timeout and retries, and makes a column required in steps
when: Migrates the rename of Board.title at expand on a table with 100 rows and completes its backfill. A test session holds an ACCESS SHARE lock on the table for the whole run of the contract step while a reader of the table runs under a statement timeout of 2.5 s; then the session holds the lock for about 1.5 s, and the contract step migrates again. Then, on a second database, the sync trigger is gone and the old column is still there: the test runs the statements of the step up to DROP TRIGGER by hand and keeps the completeness CHECK, checks the schema manifest of the release of the rename after ADD CONSTRAINT and after DROP TRIGGER, and the contract step migrates. Then, on a third database, a run before stopped after ADD CONSTRAINT committed, and the contract step migrates.
then: Expects the first run to wait for its lock 10 times, for at least 10 s, to fail, to write no ledger row and to leave the trigger and the old column; the reader to get its rows each time; the second run to succeed with the ledger row last, the new column NOT NULL and no CHECK of the change left; the release of the rename to accept the NOT NULL CHECK NOT VALID and the schema with no trigger; the rerun on the second database to run the check in full, pass it and finish with no error for the trigger that is already gone; and the rerun on the third database to add no second CHECK, validate it and finish with no CHECK left.

title: The runtime pool is opened through tenant.Open with the adapter's verified TLS configuration

Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, with TLS that the check turns on with a certificate of its own CA, and a local SpiceDB serve container of the pinned image authzed/spicedb:v1.57.0 with a memory datastore, without privilege, which the test starts and removes; a missing server fails the test. Each pool of the service comes from tenant.Open with the adapter's TenantConfig, and command.New and query.New refuse a pool that tenant.Open did not give (ST-SUP-RP10-LC30), so a started service has tenant.Opened pools. The check reads pg_stat_ssl for each connection of the runtime role, starts the service with sslmode disable and runs the migration job with sslmode prefer, each with no loopback test mode. Mutations caught: no key in 001_initial, no unique key on the referenced table, the key without the tenant column, a key that checks an unset reference.

title: A within step adds the key NOT VALID, validates it in its own migration, and stops on a row that breaks it
when: Migrates withinbase and writes as a superuser a ticket of core in the sprint of core and a ticket of web in the sprint of core; runs the migration job of within, whose step ticket-sprint-within holds sprint_id within the optional field project_id; then sets the sprint of the bad ticket to none and runs the job again; then writes as the runtime role a ticket of web in the sprint of core, and a ticket in a sprint with no project.
then: Expects the first job refused with a refusal that names step_0001_ticket-sprint-within_expand_validate, tickets_sprint_id_within_fkey and public.tickets and holds no row value, the key present and NOT VALID, the index and keys migrations in the ledger and the validate migration not; the second job to validate the key and the CHECK tickets_sprint_id_wcheck with its ledger row; the ticket of web refused with 23503 on the key, and the ticket with no project refused with 23514 on the CHECK.
notes: Level: integration. TestTables generates the module and runs the case of testdata/table_steps_test.go (TestTableSteps) there. The validate migration checks each row past row-level security (ST-SUP-RP04-LC10). PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names (ST-STD-LOCAL). Mutations caught: the key added before the unique key it refers to, the key added valid in one step, a refusal that names no key or holds a value, a key validated over a row that breaks it.

title: The within step builds the unique key, then adds the foreign key NOT VALID, then validates it, each in its own migration

notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestWithinKeys; its subtest carries this ID. Mutations caught: the key in the step migration before the index, no keys migration, no validate migration, the key in the baseline of a step.

title: The composite key of a reference to its own entity, or across the tenant column, is refused
when: Generates withinfresh with a reference parent_id of Ticket to Ticket held within project_id; then withinfresh with Project and Sprint shared.
then: Expects each generation refused, naming the reference to its own entity, and the two entities of which only one holds the tenant column.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestWithinKeys; its subtest carries this ID. A key onto its own table would refer to a unique key that its CREATE TABLE does not hold yet, and a key across the tenant column cannot match a unique key. Mutations caught: either case generated.

title: A reference held within an optional field gets a CHECK that the field is set when the reference is set, and one held within a required field gets none
when: Generates withinopt, whose Ticket holds sprint_id within the optional field project_id, and withinreq, where project_id is required.
then: Expects 001_initial of withinopt to hold CONSTRAINT tickets_sprint_id_wcheck CHECK ("sprint_id" IS NULL OR "project_id" IS NOT NULL) and its schema manifest the CHECK as pg_get_constraintdef writes it; and 001_initial of withinreq to hold the composite key and no wcheck.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestWithinKeys; its subtest carries this ID. The PostgreSQL proof is in ST-SUP-RC01-OC46-T01 and T02. Security review of PR #413, L1 and L2: MATCH SIMPLE checks no key that holds a NULL, so without the CHECK a writer outside the collection whose scope field is the within field could refer to a row of another ancestor.

title: A field whose foreign key takes the name of the composite key of a within is refused at generation, naming both
when: Generates withinfresh with one more optional reference sprint_id_within of Ticket to Sprint, whose foreign key takes the name tickets_sprint_id_within_fkey; then generates withinfresh as it is.
then: Expects the first generation to fail with an error that names tickets_sprint_id_within_fkey, the foreign key of the columns tenant_id and sprint_id_within, and the foreign key of the columns tenant_id, project_id and sprint_id. Expects 001_initial of the second to hold the constraint tickets_sprint_id_within_fkey, with its name as before.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestNamesApart; its subtest carries this ID. Security review of PR #413, I1: the plain key of a field named <reference>_within took the name of the within key, and PostgreSQL refused the migration only when it ran. Generation now refuses two constraints of a table, or two tables or indexes of the schema, with one name. The name of the within key does not change, because a database that applied a within step holds that name and the ledger has no place for a rename migration (see sec-417 L2).

title: The migrations of a drop keep the old column or table at expand and drop it at contract with short statements

title: A secret column is bytea or text with no CHECK and no index, and the re-seal statements take the tenant

title: The expand of a seal adds the sealed column beside the clear one, and the contract checks and drops the clear column

title: A seal at expand keeps the release before working, the seal job seals each row, and a roll back to the release before loses no write

Runs in the generated module of TestTables (testdata/seal_steps_test.go) on the local PostgreSQL container that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names, with a throwaway key ring in memory (ST-STD-LOCAL). Walkthrough 13, W13-B1: code is a secret that a generator before postgres-adapter 6.13.0 stored in clear.

title: A head that seals a stored field with a seal change is accepted against the base at expand and at contract

then: Expects the first contract refused with a refusal that names this database instance and the remedy to build the release of the expand step again with postgres-adapter 6.21.0, seal_instance then to hold the table identity of this release, the first run of the seal job to wait, the contract then refused because no pass completed, the next run of the seal job to complete a new pass, and the contract then to pass.

title: The check of a seal contract runs the functions of this release in its own transaction, also when another job put older functions in place after the start of the job
when: On a database with the seals at expand and a completed pass, holds the ledger lock on a connection of the test and runs the migration job of the contract release: each time that the job waits at a transaction lock of the ledger, gives the lock to it and asks for it again; when the job waits at the session lock of the contract step, after the run of the seal checkpoints at its start, puts the seal_instance of postgres-adapter 6.20.0 in place and gives the lock to the job.

Mutation caught: no run of the seal checkpoints in the check transaction of the contract step (the job then refuses, because the older seal_instance gives another database instance). Security review of PR #472, second review, L1.

title: A changed body of an applied migration is refused with a fault that names it
given: The generated storage package of the runtime data path, migrated on a local PostgreSQL server.

title: The emitted backend sets a strict active session cookie
when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers, restarts the backend, then signs out.

when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers, restarts the backend, then signs out.

title: The emitted store encrypts session records and binds them to the cookie hash
when: Creates a session with an access and a refresh token, then reads the stored row and opens the record with another cookie ID and with one changed byte.
then: Expects a 32-byte hash, no plaintext token and no raw cookie ID in the row, and refusal of both the foreign cookie ID and the changed ciphertext.

title: The emitted session response holds no tokens
when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers, restarts the backend, then signs out.
then: Expects the login cookie Lax and the active cookie Strict, both Secure, HttpOnly and host-only, no token in the session response, only the server access token and four permitted headers at the API, and no upstream Set-Cookie.

title: The emitted backend refuses a mutation without an exact origin or a CSRF token
when: Sends thirteen requests with a missing, wrong, repeated or same-site origin, a missing or repeated CSRF header, a browser bearer token, a duplicate cookie, a bad method and an oversize body.
then: Expects the stated status for each case, and expects that no denied request reached the API.

title: The emitted backend refuses browser bearer credentials
when: Sends thirteen requests with a missing, wrong, repeated or same-site origin, a missing or repeated CSRF header, a browser bearer token, a duplicate cookie, a bad method and an oversize body.
then: Expects the stated status for each case, and expects that no denied request reached the API.

title: A captured asset refuses a browser bearer token
when: Reads each captured path from two backends with a session and a browser bearer token, among the other captured asset reads.
then: Expects 400 for each read that carries the bearer token.
notes: Conditional: the test skips when its fixture carries no captured assets, so whether it runs depends on the fixture rather than on the environment. Another test in the same folder takes the opposite branch, so both fixture shapes exist. Whether the default fixture reaches this test is not settled; check it before this proof is relied on.

title: The local application proxy refuses a browser bearer token
when: Sends an authenticated application request with a browser bearer token, among the other denied requests.
then: Expects 400.

title: The emitted proxy sends only server-held credentials
when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers and each header of the allow list, then with Idempotency-Key two times, restarts the backend, then signs out.
then: Expects the login cookie Lax and the active cookie Strict, both Secure, HttpOnly and host-only, no token in the session response, only the server access token and the headers of the allow list at the API (Accept, Content-Type, If-Match, If-None-Match, Idempotency-Key, Authz-Revocation-After and Prefer wait=4, each as sent), no Cookie, Origin, CSRF, trace or other browser header, the response headers Idempotent-Replayed, Authz-Revocation, Authz-Revocation-Location and Preference-Applied at the browser, 400 for the key given two times, and no upstream Set-Cookie.
notes: Walkthrough 8 (W8-B3): the proxy sent only four headers, so no STEGO command worked through a browser service (400 idempotency-key-missing). The allow list is named in the README of the component, and the client of the proxy (httpclient.RenderProxy) sends Idempotency-Key, which the other HTTPS clients refuse.

title: Only the clients of the API proxy, of the CLI and of the Go SDK send Idempotency-Key; the other HTTPS clients refuse it
given: The client of httpclient.Render, the client of httpclient.RenderProxy the client of httpclient.RenderCLI and the client of httpclient.RenderSDK, each in a module of its own, and an HTTPS test server.
when: Sends a POST with Idempotency-Key through each client, then one with X-Idempotency-Key, then a PATCH with the key, then a GET, a PUT, a DELETE and a HEAD with the key.
then: Expects the clients of the proxy, of the CLI and of the Go SDK to send the key as given on the POST and the PATCH, the other client to refuse the request before it is sent, and each client to refuse X-Idempotency-Key; on the GET, PUT, DELETE and HEAD, the client of the proxy to send the key as the browser gives it, and the clients of the CLI, of the Go SDK and the other client to refuse the request before it is sent.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestIdempotencyKeyClients; its subtest carries this ID. The security review of PR 422 (I5) asked for it, so that the boundary holds for the SDK and HTTP application clients. The CLI client sends the key that the CLI makes, because the CLI sends a write again only with the same key (ST-SUP-RC04-OC31, ST-SUP-Q187). Mutation caught: RenderCLI with a client that refuses the key. Security review of PR #447, I-3: the CLI client sends the key only on a POST and a PATCH. Mutation caught: RenderCLI with a client that sends the key on every method.

title: A request that waits for a revocation asks for a wait below the proxy timeout and holds only a slot of its own pool and of its session
given: The generated backend with signed-in sessions and a test API that keeps each request with Authz-Revocation-After and a wait other than wait=0, as a pending revocation does.
when: Sends reads with each form of Prefer, with and without Authz-Revocation-After; then keeps one waiting read of each of as many sessions as the wait pool has slots at the API and sends one more waiting read of another session; releases them; then keeps one waiting read of one session and sends a second waiting read of the same session and a waiting read of another session; then a read that does not wait; then answers Authz-Revocation-Location with an absolute URL, a path with no identity and another path.
then: Expects the API to get only wait=N, at most 4, and wait=4 for a waiting read with no valid wait, and no Prefer for other preferences; the read past the full pool and the second read of the one session answered 201 at once with wait=0 sent to the API, never 503; the read of the other session kept in the pool; each kept read answered after the release; the read that does not wait served; and no Authz-Revocation-Location at the browser for the three bad values.
notes: Level: integration. TestGeneratedRuntime runs it in the generated module against the local PostgreSQL server. The security review of PR 422 found M1 (a waiting read held the shared proxy slots and got 502 after the 5 s timeout), L1 (Authz-Revocation-Location was not checked) and L2 (Prefer was sent as a whole). The security review of PR 440 found L2: writes now wait too, and one session that loops on a pending revocation took the pool of the other users and gave them 503; now a session holds at most MaxWaitsPerSession (1) slot, and a request past a limit goes on with wait=0, as the service does over its waiter limits.

title: Two emitted backend instances share one token renewal
when: Expires the access token, holds the provider refresh request, then asks for the session from both backend instances.
then: Expects the second instance to wait, both requests to succeed, the new access token at the API, and exactly one refresh request.

title: A second backend renews an expired application session
when: Expires the access token, then sends an application request through a second backend instance.
then: Expects success, and expects the application to receive the renewed access token.

title: A waiter for an active renewal has a deadline and keeps its cookie
when: Claims a renewal, then asks for the session, then asks again with a cancelled context.
then: Expects 503 with Retry-After inside three seconds, a retained session cookie, a cancelled waiter that stops inside one second, and no use of the refresh token.

title: A lost or stale renewal requires a new login and is not retried
when: Drops the provider refresh response, and separately ages an existing refresh claim past its deadline, then sends two API requests.
then: Expects 401 for both requests and expects no second refresh request.

title: A renewal claim with a lost commit requires a new login
when: Expires the access token, then loses the commit of the renewal claim.
then: Expects a session error, no stored session, and no provider refresh request.

title: A completed renewal cannot restore a session that sign-out removed
when: Starts a renewal on one instance, holds the provider request, then signs out on the second instance and releases the renewal.
then: Expects the sign-out to succeed, the later API request to return 401, and both the old and the rotated token to be revoked.

title: A renewal that spans a key switch cannot restore a signed-out session
when: Reads one old record through four key rings, writes through two mixed writers, then signs out during a key switch.
then: Expects every listed key to decrypt, the first key to encrypt new records, a removed key to lose access, and a renewal after sign-out to fail.

title: An application sign-out on one backend ends the session on another
when: Signs out without a CSRF token, then with one, and reads through a second backend instance after each.
then: Expects the first sign-out refused with the session kept, and 401 on the second backend after the valid sign-out.

title: The sign-out confirmation page does not sign out
when: Opens the confirmation page, then posts the form with a missing, null, foreign or repeated Origin value and with four invalid bodies.
then: Expects the page to keep the session and revoke nothing, Referrer-Policy same-origin on that page and no-referrer elsewhere, 403 or 400 for each invalid form, and sign-out only after a valid form.

title: The sign-out confirmation page does not sign out under native browser navigation
when: Opens the confirmation page in a headless browser with a session cookie and presses its submit button, once with the generated referrer policy and once with a no-referrer control.
then: Expects the generated page to post a same-origin form that signs out and revokes the session, and the control form to be refused with the session kept.
notes: Gated: the test skips unless STEGO_REQUIRE_BROWSER_LOGOUT is 1, and then it runs only in CI with Chrome or Chromium. It gives no proof on a developer workstation.

title: The sign-out confirmation page keeps its same-origin referrer policy
when: Opens the confirmation page, then posts the form with a missing, null, foreign or repeated Origin value and with four invalid bodies.
then: Expects the page to keep the session and revoke nothing, Referrer-Policy same-origin on that page and no-referrer elsewhere, 403 or 400 for each invalid form, and sign-out only after a valid form.

title: The sign-out confirmation page lets a native form send its Origin
when: Opens the confirmation page in a headless browser with a session cookie and presses its submit button, once with the generated referrer policy and once with a no-referrer control.
then: Expects the same-origin policy to send the page origin, and the no-referrer control to send a null Origin.
notes: Gated: the test skips unless STEGO_REQUIRE_BROWSER_LOGOUT is 1, and then it runs only in CI with Chrome or Chromium. It gives no proof on a developer workstation.

title: The emitted provider sign-out refuses unsafe endpoints
when: Builds the provider sign-out target for six unsafe discovered endpoints and for one valid HTTPS endpoint.

title: The emitted script hashes apply only to the index document
when: Requests each declared route and asset, three undeclared paths, five unsafe return paths, and a plaintext or wrong-host address.
then: Expects a policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, the script hashes only on index.html, 404 for each undeclared path, / for each unsafe return path, and 400 for the wrong host.

title: The emitted backend refuses an identity host that shares the console cookie host
when: Starts the backend with an issuer on the console host and another port, then with a discovered authorization endpoint on the console host.

when: Starts the backend with eight invalid upstream addresses, four of them on the console host.
then: Expects each start to fail.

title: The emitted key reader accepts only a small ring of distinct canonical keys
when: Reads four valid key files, then twenty-six invalid files with bad size, bad base64, a duplicate key, four keys, unknown or repeated JSON fields and trailing data.
then: Expects the valid files to keep their key order, and expects every invalid file to return the fixed error with a nil key ring.

title: The emitted backend checks its key file before database or provider access
when: Starts the backend with a key ring that repeats one key and with no database connection, among the other key switch steps.
then: Expects startup to fail with a key error.

title: The emitted store keeps old sessions readable across a key rollout
when: Reads one old record through four key rings, writes through two mixed writers, then signs out during a key switch.
then: Expects every listed key to decrypt, the first key to encrypt new records, a removed key to lose access, and a renewal after sign-out to fail.

title: A backend key switch keeps the browser session
when: Starts one backend with the old key first and one with the new key first, reads the session from each, then signs out on one.
then: Expects both backends to read the session, and the old writer not to restore it after sign-out.

title: The emitted backend reduces unsafe return paths to the root route
when: Requests each declared route and asset, three undeclared paths, five unsafe return paths, and a plaintext or wrong-host address.
then: Expects a policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, the script hashes only on index.html, 404 for each undeclared path, / for each unsafe return path, and 400 for the wrong host.

title: The completion document reduces an unsafe return target to the root route
when: Renders the completion document for nine return targets: local, a quoted query, absolute, a network path, an auth route, a fragment, an encoded path, a header injection and an over-long path.
then: Expects the safe targets to stay, and every unsafe target to become the root route.

title: The emitted backend returns 404 for undeclared paths
when: Requests each declared route and asset, three undeclared paths, five unsafe return paths, and a plaintext or wrong-host address.
then: Expects a policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, the script hashes only on index.html, 404 for each undeclared path, / for each unsafe return path, and 400 for the wrong host.

title: The local application proxy returns 404 for an undeclared UI route
when: Requests an undeclared UI route with a valid session, among the other denied requests.
then: Expects 404.

title: A storage failure reports temporary unavailability and keeps the cookie
when: Closes the database, then asks for the session.
then: Expects 503 with Retry-After 1 and no Set-Cookie header.

title: The emitted callback consumes a pending login exactly once
when: Sends a callback with a wrong state, then sends the same valid callback from two backend instances at the same time.
then: Expects no code exchange for the wrong state, one success and one denial for the concurrent pair, and exactly one exchange.

title: A rejected identity token gets no session and is revoked
when: Completes a callback for eight provider modes with a bad nonce, issuer, audience, expiry, issue time, auth time, roles or access token hash.
then: Expects 502 for each mode, no session cookie, and eight token revocations.

when: Sends an API request with no session, then with a session the upstream rejects, then repeats it.
then: Expects the fixed 401 body, the WWW-Authenticate and no-store headers, no forwarded Location or ETag, a cleared cookie, and one upstream call.

title: The completion document holds no private state
when: Completes a protected application callback, then replays the same callback.
then: Expects a Strict, Secure, HttpOnly, host-only cookie, no session ID, token, code or state in the body, and 400 with no document for the replay.

title: The completion document holds no active markup and keeps its privacy headers
when: Renders the completion document for nine safe and unsafe return targets.
then: Expects one refresh and one link, no script, no cookie, no-store, no referrer, and a policy that permits no active or framed content.

title: Each index document gets a fresh style nonce
when: Requests the index document three times with dynamic styles enabled, then an asset, then an invalid insertion offset.
then: Expects three distinct 32-byte nonces that match their own document and policy, a changed ETag each time, no nonce on the asset, and a closed failure for the bad offset.

title: The runtime refuses a changed grant on its session table
when: Adds a schema CREATE grant, adds a grant option, and removes the DELETE grant.
then: Expects both Verify and Bootstrap to refuse each case.

title: The runtime login of the managed schema has only data access
when: Sets up the schema, then runs data statements and four schema statements as the runtime login.
then: Expects the data statements to succeed and each schema statement to be denied with code 42501.

then: Expects a fresh response, the escaped stego-runtime-config element, a disabled export for a missing collector, and the same content security policy.

title: The authorization request keeps the declared scopes
when: Starts login with one declared scope and then with four declared scopes.
then: Expects the authorization request's scope parameter to equal the declared value each time.

title: An API permission denial does not end a valid session
when: Makes the upstream API answer 403, then 401.
then: Expects the session to stay authenticated after the 403 and to end after the 401.

title: The pending login limit is enforced
when: Inserts 1,000 pending logins with one bounded statement, then creates one more.
then: Expects the store error and exactly 1,000 remaining records.

title: A cross-site request cannot read a private response
when: Sends the public page and three private routes with a cross-site and then a same-site fetch site, holding a valid cookie.
then: Expects 200 for the public page and 403 for the session, login and API routes.

when: Reads seven invalid documents with a repeated name, a lone surrogate, trailing data or deep nesting, then three valid documents.
then: Expects every invalid document refused and every valid document accepted.

then: Expects 304, an empty body and the upstream ETag.

when: Sends seven ingest requests with a missing session, missing CSRF token, missing Origin, wrong media type, wrong method, unknown path or oversize body, then a browser bearer token and compressed input.
then: Expects the stated status for each case and expects no telemetry at the API.

when: Takes six admissions for one session, then one more, then fills the session map and asks for another session.
then: Expects the six admissions, the refusal after them, and a 512-entry bound on the map.

when: Takes two sockets for one session and then a third, ends the session, fills the backend capacity, then closes the set.
then: Expects the busy error for the third session socket, the cancellation on end, the busy error at backend capacity, and no socket after close.

title: A socket upgrade needs a session and an exact origin
when: Dials the socket route without a session, with a wrong Origin, with no Origin, with a browser bearer token, and with a denied query.

title: A socket survives the HTTP deadlines and relays both message kinds
when: Opens a socket through a server with 80 ms deadlines, waits 120 ms, then relays a binary and a text message and ends the session.
then: Expects both messages returned without a change, the exit status in the close reason, and a 101 upgrade status in the telemetry wrapper.

title: Every session end closes that session's sockets
when: Ends the session through local sign-out, remote sign-out, backend close, runtime stop, a storage failure, session expiry and token expiry.
then: Expects the socket to close in each mode and expects no socket lease to remain.
notes: Gated: the test needs a database and skips unless STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names one. It therefore gives no proof on a developer workstation, and proves its contracts only in a run that sets the variable. Lathe counts it as automated, which does not distinguish a test that runs from one that skips.

title: The socket data budget counts messages, bytes and empty frames
when: Offers data at the message bound, at the byte bound, an empty message at the last slot, and one oversize message.
then: Expects a refusal at each bound, the empty message counted, and the oversize message refused.

title: The local application proxy drops every untrusted browser header
when: Sends authenticated application requests, and a second backend's requests, with a cookie and four client-supplied identity headers.
then: Expects the server access token at the application, all five untrusted headers absent, and no private header in the response.

when: Checks a write request with four untrusted fetch site values, with no Origin, then with the exact Origin.
then: Expects only the exact Origin with no untrusted fetch site to pass.

title: An anonymous document request starts login and keeps the cookie
when: Requests an API path and an asset with no session, a declared route by direct navigation, then the landing page cross-site.
then: Expects 401 for the private paths, a 303 to the login route for the document, the sign-in page cross-site, and no Set-Cookie header.

title: A captured asset needs a session and stops after sign-out
when: Reads each captured path from two backends with a session, anonymously, conditionally, with a browser bearer token, then after sign-out.
then: Expects no-store and no token in every body, 401 for an anonymous read, 400 for the bearer token, and 401 on the second backend after sign-out.
notes: Conditional: the test skips when its fixture carries no captured assets, so whether it runs depends on the fixture rather than on the environment. Another test in the same folder takes the opposite branch, so both fixture shapes exist. Whether the default fixture reaches this test is not settled; check it before this proof is relied on.

title: Schema setup is locked and repeatable
when: Runs two owner connections through Bootstrap at the same time, repeats the setup, then runs data and schema statements as the runtime login.
then: Expects both owners to succeed, an unchanged catalog snapshot after the repeat, the four data statements to pass, and four schema statements to be denied.

title: A failed schema setup rolls back
when: Adds an unsafe default table grant and runs Bootstrap, then removes the grant and runs Bootstrap again.
then: Expects the first setup to fail and leave no table, and the second setup to succeed.

title: Startup refuses a schema that differs from the generated one
when: Changes the table, a column, a constraint or an index, then verifies the schema.
then: Expects the runtime to refuse startup for each change.

title: Schema setup refuses invalid input
when: Calls Verify and Bootstrap with a nil context, a nil connection and an unsafe role name.
then: Expects the fixed schema error for each call.

title: Startup diagnostics name each stage and hold no private input
when: Runs the generated runtime in a child process for six failure points and one success, with private markers in every configuration value.
then: Expects one completion record per stage in order, the correct outcome for the last stage, only the ten permitted fields, and no private marker in the output.

title: A startup step keeps its error, its context and its panic
when: Runs a startup step for a nil error, a cancellation, a deadline and a private error, then one that panics.
then: Expects the same error value, exactly one call, the caller's own context, and the panic passed through unchanged.

title: A failed renewal claim leaves the session usable
when: Injects a lost row, a cancellation and a deadline at the claim read, then renews the session again.
then: Expects the store error, an active session with its original credentials, no refresh token use, and one successful later renewal.

title: A cancelled renewal leaves no refresh claim
when: Pauses the provider inside the renewal, then cancels the caller.
then: Expects the renewal to fail and expects no retained refresh claim in the store.

title: The mode migrate runs Bootstrap as the owner for the named runtime login, with no runtime credential
given: A test database owned by a NOLOGIN owner role, a runtime login with only CONNECT and USAGE, the fixture's administrator login, and a plain migration login made in the test as a member of the owner role; the loopback test mode of the database connection; no DATABASE_URL.
when: Calls schema.Migrate with the administrator's owner connection and STEGO_RUNTIME_DATABASE_ROLE empty, bad;role and Upper; then with the runtime login's name and no STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL; then with the member login's connection, twice; then writes a session row as the runtime login; then calls it with an owner connection string that does not open.
then: Expects the three role names refused at the stage service.start.setting.browser-backend.STEGO_RUNTIME_DATABASE_ROLE; the missing owner setting refused at its stage with no schema made; both runs of the member login to pass through SET ROLE, Verify as the runtime login to pass and the row to be written; and the last call refused at database.access with no password in the error.

title: A browser-service gets the mode migrate in main.go and the migration Job with the owner Secret and the runtime role name in its base
given: The scaffold of stego init --archetype browser-service.
when: Runs stego apply and reads out/main.go, deploy/base/migration-job.yaml, deploy/base/deployment.yaml and deploy/platform-requirements.yaml.
then: Expects main.go to run schema.Migrate for the one argument migrate with the stage of schema.Stage, to run schema.Verify at the stage database.schema before the stage database.access, and its failure record to name the fault class; the migration Job to run migrate with STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL from the key url of the Secret greeter-database-owner and STEGO_RUNTIME_DATABASE_ROLE, and with no DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL_FILE or runtime database Secret (ST-DLV-INV13); the Deployment not to read the owner Secret; and the platform requirements to name it.
notes: Level: system. The real use is in the core8 proof of PR notes: migrate, start, sign-in redirect and a broken schema against PostgreSQL.

title: The database setup of the browser-backend README, run as it is written, passes the mode migrate and Verify
given: The generated browser service of the browser-backend fixture, the README of the component copied beside the test, and a local PostgreSQL server whose administrator connection is STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN.
when: Reads the three SQL blocks and the one psql block of the README, fills <service> with a new value, and runs them in the order of the README, statement by statement: the first SQL block on the server as the administrator; the psql block, whose SHOW password_encryption runs as SQL and whose lines \password <role> each set a new secret of that role as psql does; the second SQL block, which revokes CONNECT on postgres and template1, on the server; and the third in the new database. Then runs the mode migrate twice with only STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL of the migration login and STEGO_RUNTIME_DATABASE_ROLE, Verify as the runtime login, and a connection of the runtime login to each of the databases postgres and template1.
then: Expects no SQL statement of the README to hold a secret, SHOW password_encryption to give scram-sha-256, the psql block to set the secrets of the runtime and the migration login and no other, each README statement to run, each run of the mode migrate to pass, Verify of the runtime login to pass, and each connection to postgres and template1 to be refused for want of permission.
notes: Level: service. Proved by TestGeneratedBrowserSchemaMigrate of internal/generator/browserbackend/generator_test.go, which builds the generated module and runs this test. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege. Walkthrough 7, B4: with the roles as the README stated them, the mode migrate failed with fault owner, because PostgreSQL makes a role INHERIT by default and the README gave the migration login CONNECT. The README now gives the exact SQL, and this test keeps it true. Security review of PR #415 (sec-415 L3): the README gave literal passwords in its SQL, which go to the shell history and the server log, and left the CONNECT of PUBLIC on the default database postgres. The README now sets each secret with \password of psql, which sends only its SCRAM hash, and revokes that CONNECT. Security review of PR #420 (LOW-1, LOW-2): the server-wide REVOKE is its own block after the warning about other logins, it covers template1 too, the README names pg_hba.conf as the real limit, and the psql block first shows that password_encryption is scram-sha-256. The test restores the CONNECT of PUBLIC on postgres and template1, which other tests of the server use.

title: A service name whose database logins are longer than 63 bytes is refused, naming the login
given: The browser-backend fixture.
when: Runs the mode migrate with STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL of the old owner login. Then reads the three SQL blocks and the one psql block of the section 'Move a browser-service database to the owner and migrator logins', fills <service>, and runs them in their order, statement by statement: the first SQL block on the server as the administrator, the psql block as psql does, the second SQL block in the database, and each query of the third block in the database. Then runs the mode migrate twice with the migration login, Verify as the runtime login, a count of the sessions as the runtime login, and a connection of the old owner login. Proved by the check of this ID in internal/generator/restapi/testdata/crud_test.go, which TestCrudService of internal/generator/restapi/runtime_data_test.go builds with the Go of STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO against the runtime module of this repository and runs over HTTPS; TestCrudService generates the CLI and builds it as a program, which the check runs. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL in a local container without privilege, given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, and a local SpiceDB serve container of the pinned image without privilege. ST-SUP-Q187, decision (b). Mutations caught: the CLI sends no key (each create answered 400); the resource does not state IdempotentWrites (the apply of lost gave the status unknown).

title: A refused service certificate is ErrUntrusted and not a transport failure, and a server that does not answer is ErrTransport
given: The HTTPS client of RenderCLI in a module of the test, a TLS test server that answers 204 and counts its requests, whose certificate names 127.0.0.1 and not localhost, and a TLS test server with a certificate that signs itself, names 127.0.0.1 and expired an hour ago, which also counts its requests.
when: Sends a POST through a client with the CA of the server and the host name localhost, a client with the system CAs, a client with the CA of the server and a PeerCertificateSHA256 of another leaf, and a client with the expired certificate as its CA; then through a client that trusts the server; then to a TLS server that is closed.
then: Expects ErrUntrusted, and not ErrTransport or ErrDeadline, for each of the four refused certificates, and no request at a server; 204 from the trusted server; and ErrTransport, not ErrUntrusted, from the closed server. So the CLI, which sends a write again only after ErrTransport, ErrDeadline or a 5xx answer, does not send a write again after a refused certificate.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestUntrustedServiceCertificate in internal/generator/httpclient/render_test.go, which runs it in the module of the generated client. Security review of PR #449, INFO-3: a TLS verification failure counted as ErrTransport, so the CLI sent the write again. http-application 2.2.0. Security review of PR #456, I5: no case of an expired certificate; added by fu/standing-23. Mutations caught (fu/standing-22): no ErrUntrusted case (all three gave ErrTransport); no match of the pin error (the pin case gave ErrTransport). Mutations caught (fu/standing-23): untrusted false for a certificate error with the reason Expired (the expired case gave ErrTransport); a certificate that is not expired (the request reached the server).

title: A handshake alert from the service on a new connection, such as for a client certificate that it requires, is ErrUntrusted and not a transport failure
given: The HTTPS client of RenderCLI in a module of the test, with no client certificate, and a TLS test server that requires a client certificate and counts the requests that it handles; the CA file of the client holds the certificate of the server.
when: Sends a POST with a body through the client.
then: Expects ErrUntrusted, and not ErrTransport or ErrDeadline: the server refuses the TLS session on a new connection with the alert certificate required, which the client gets as a net.OpError with the Op remote error; and no request handled at the server. So the CLI does not send a write again after a TLS session that the service refused.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestServiceTLSAlert in internal/generator/httpclient/render_test.go, which runs it in the module of the generated client. Security review of PR #456, I1: a TLS alert from the server, such as an mTLS refusal of the client, stayed ErrTransport, so the CLI sent the write one time again. crypto/tls gives a remote alert as a net.OpError with an unexported alert value, not as tls.AlertError (that wraps only the alerts of QUIC and the alerts that the client sends). Security review of PR #458, L1: only a handshake or certificate alert on a new connection is ErrUntrusted (ST-SUP-RC04-OC31-T05). http-application 2.3.0. Mutations caught (fu/standing-23): untrusted with no match of the remote error (ErrTransport); no class of a session alert (ErrTransport).

title: A TLS alert on a reused connection, or one that is not a handshake or certificate alert, is ErrTransport
given: The HTTPS client of RenderCLI in a module of the test, whose TLS dial the test replaces with a dial of a plain test server that answers 204, through a connection that, once the test sets an alert text, gives each read as a net.OpError with the Op remote error and that text, as crypto/tls gives a TLS alert from the service.
when: For each of the alerts certificate required, bad record MAC and internal error: sends a POST that passes, sets the alert, and sends a POST again on the reused connection. Then, for certificate required, handshake failure, bad record MAC and internal error, sends a POST on a new connection whose alert is set before the first read.
then: Expects ErrTransport, and not ErrUntrusted, for each alert on a reused connection, because it can come after the service read the request; ErrUntrusted for certificate required and handshake failure on a new connection; and ErrTransport for bad record MAC and internal error on a new connection. So ErrUntrusted, which tells that the service did not do the request, is given only when that is true.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestServiceTLSAlertReused in internal/generator/httpclient/render_test.go, which runs it in the module of the generated client. Security review of PR #458, L1: each fatal TLS alert was ErrUntrusted, also one on a reused connection after the request was written, so the text that the certificate is not trusted and the doc claim that the service did not do the request could be false, and a user could send the write again by hand. The client takes the reuse from httptrace GotConnInfo.Reused. http-application 2.3.0. Mutations caught (fu/standing-23): untrusted with reused always false (certificate required on a reused connection gave ErrUntrusted); GotConn that does not record the reuse (the same); a match of each remote alert with no alert text (bad record MAC and internal error on a new connection gave ErrUntrusted).
