title: The emitted runtime opens its watch before the first scan
when: Runs the controller with a source whose scan emits one live record and one retained deletion record.
then: Expects the watch open before the scan, no parallel action, and both typed items in order.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC05-OC02-T01.

title: The emitted runtime runs serial actions in queue order
when: Runs the controller with a source whose scan emits one live record and one retained deletion record.
then: Expects the watch open before the scan, no parallel action, and both typed items in order.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC05-OC01-T01.

title: Queue overflow cancels the session, joins its workers and rescans
when: Fills the bounded queue while one action is active, then lets the recovery session run.
then: Expects the active action canceled, every worker joined, a second watch session, and a new scan after it.

title: A denied operation stops the runtime and is not hidden
when: Denies the watch, then the scan, then the action, in three separate runs.
then: Expects the denial from Run in each run, and exactly one watch attempt.

title: Invalid options open no source
when: Runs the controller with six option sets, each with one invalid capacity, policy, interval or timeout.
then: Expects an error for each set, and no call to the source.

title: Watch setup has the operation deadline
when: Keeps the first watch setup open until its context ends, then denies the second setup.
then: Expects the setup to time out, a second attempt, the denial from Run, and no scan after a failed setup.

title: An action deadline is reported and its workers are joined
when: Runs the controller with a 5 ms action timeout and an action that waits for its context.
then: Expects the observed reconcile_failed error to be context.DeadlineExceeded, and expects the scans to stop before Run returns.

title: A new event cannot bypass a failed key's retry delay
when: Fails one key, adds it 1,000 times, takes a healthy key, and then takes the failed key after its delay.
then: Expects the unchanged due time, progress for the healthy key, the retry only after its due time, and a delay that grows to the configured cap.

title: Keyed workers keep independent progress and serialize each key
when: Runs a keyed watch controller with two workers and repeated events for two keys.
then: Expects at most one active action for each key, and concurrent progress for the other key.

title: A pending result keeps its capacity and its delay
when: Finishes one key with a one-hour recheck, adds that key again three times, restarts the queue, and then fills the capacity.
then: Expects no retry count for the pending key, the same due time after the events and the restart, an overflow error at the capacity bound, and progress for another key.

title: The scanner checks a whole page before any effect
when: Returns six pages with an empty cursor, a repeated cursor, invalid UTF-8, an oversized cursor, too many items, and an empty continuation.
then: Expects ErrScanContract for each page and zero emitter calls.

title: A slow stream cannot starve retained history
when: Runs one sweep group whose first stream holds its action until the pass budget ends, with a history stream after it.
then: Expects the history stream to run and its terminal error to stop the sweep.

title: The emitted process keeps domain text and goroutine dumps out of its output
when: Runs the generated process as a subprocess for a signal, a callback failure, three panic forms, a runtime.Goexit and a panic in a defer.
then: Expects exit code 1 with one fixed failure record for each fault, no private credential and no goroutine dump in the output, the cleanup marker written, and a clean exit after SIGTERM.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC05-OC14-T01.

title: The emitted process exits with code 1 and one fixed failure record after its cleanup
when: Runs the generated process as a subprocess for a signal, a callback failure, three panic forms, a runtime.Goexit and a panic in a defer.
then: Expects exit code 1 with one fixed failure record for each fault, no private credential and no goroutine dump in the output, the cleanup marker written, and a clean exit after SIGTERM.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC05-OC13-T01.

title: A cycle keeps its failure across process replacement
when: Fails one action in the first cycle, then completes the cycle with a new call, and then runs two more cycles.
then: Expects the failure and ErrCycleFailed, the retained failure for the completed cycle, no provider error text in the checkpoint, and a new full cycle after it.

title: Run owns its telemetry and excludes private data
when: Runs the public entry point with a TLS collector, a private resource value and private callback errors, with sampling enabled and disabled.
then: Expects independent operation roots, provider spans under them, the bounded queue counts, complete flush, and no private value in any exported batch or local log.

title: An uncertain save requires a fresh load
when: Saves with a lost result, a wrong version and a mutated argument.
then: Expects no usable state and one write for each fault, and the saved value after a fresh load.

title: A slow scan finishes without an overlapping scan
when: Runs the controller with a scan that needs more time than the resync interval.
then: Expects no overlapping scan and the emitted item from the slow scan.

title: A transient action failure is recovered by the next scan
when: Fails the first action with an I/O error, then denies the second attempt.
then: Expects two attempts and the terminal error from the second one.

title: A canceled parent saves no checkpoint
when: Cancels the parent context inside the action of a checkpointed scan.
then: Expects context.Canceled and no save call.

title: An observation keeps its commit reserve
when: Runs an observation with a 300 ms parent deadline, a one-second work timeout and a 200 ms commit reserve, and returns success from the work callback after its deadline.
then: Expects the work deadline at the parent deadline less the reserve, a live commit context with the deadline error, a closed work context, and the deadline error from the call.

title: A sealed state record binds its key, its version and its bytes
when: Seals one record twice, opens it with four changed keys and another version, flips each bit in turn, and formats the protector and the value.
then: Expects no plaintext in the envelope, a new envelope for each seal, a correct round trip, a refusal for every changed key, version and damaged byte, redacted formats, and a failed JSON export.

title: The keyed queue starts paused and keeps its work
when: Adds one key before the baseline, then sets the baseline, then resets it and adds the key again.
then: Expects no take before the baseline and during the reset, and the retained key after each one.

title: An invalid key consumes no capacity
when: Adds an empty key, a 1,025-byte key and a key that is not valid UTF-8.
then: Expects ErrKey for each key and no queue entry.

title: A due retry runs before a newer key
when: Fails one key, makes its retry due, and adds a new key.
then: Expects the due retry before the new key.

title: Probe commands start no application work
when: Runs the live probe and the ready probe against a local server, then three invalid argument sets and five invalid monitor addresses.
then: Expects success for both probes with no application callback, and exit code 2 for every invalid argument and address.

title: The emitted controller uses no session advisory lock for election

notes: Level: service. Not automated yet: the registration factory is gone with the store-path bridge (2026-11-12), but no test runs a server stream through its query fill here yet. The change that takes the factory out of the runtime also deletes the factory tests in internal/generator/grpcapplication/testdata/runtime_test.go, removes ST-SUP-RC07-OC06 and ST-SUP-RC07-OC14 and records their retirement, succeeded by this contract; this specification change keeps them because their automated tests are still in the tree (ST-STD-CODE-R04); they belong to the 1.x major, and this contract to 2.0.0, so they do not contradict. Each new major MUST meet the quality bar again at its new digest before it is released as ga (ST-SUP-INV07). Decision of 2026-11-07 on the review of PR 125, under the Product owner's delegation: removing factory_package is a major change, so http-application goes to 3.0.0 and grpc-application to 2.0.0, and the old majors are superseded with a fail date. Decision on ST-SUP-Q40 (2026-11-07, under the Product owner's delegation): the gRPC application loses its registration factory as the HTTP application lost its factory, because no hand-written code runs outside a fill. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): the PostgreSQL server runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it. Decision of 2026-11-07 on the review of PR 125: each contract and invariant holds one duty. Decision on N3 of the re-check of PR 125 (2026-11-07, under the Product owner's delegation): gRPC server streams stay, each backed by a query fill with the read-only query handle and a decision on each message at the floor; client and bidirectional streams are out of scope for now and are refused. Decision of 2026-11-07 on the final check of PR 125: a server stream's lifetime is bounded.

title: The emitted readiness answers 503 before the first successful sample
when: Runs a monitor whose one check first fails with a private error text, sends 1,600 concurrent readiness requests, then makes the check pass and fail again.
then: Expects 503 before the first sample, 503 with the fixed unavailable body and no-store header while the check fails, exactly one check call for all probe traffic, 200 liveness during the failure, and readiness that follows recovery and the later failure.

title: The emitted liveness stays 200 while the dependency check fails
when: Runs a monitor whose one check first fails with a private error text, sends 1,600 concurrent readiness requests, then makes the check pass and fail again.

then: Expects the check context closed inside one second, 503 for the late success, a refusal for the second Run call, and 503 right after the parent cancellation.

title: Cancellation of the service context clears the emitted readiness
when: Runs a monitor whose check waits for its context, then calls Run again, then cancels the parent context of a second monitor that is ready.
then: Expects the check context closed inside one second, 503 for the late success, a refusal for the second Run call, and 503 right after the parent cancellation.

then: Expects the check context closed inside one second, 503 for the late success, a refusal for the second Run call, and 503 right after the parent cancellation.

title: The emitted readiness expires while a check stalls

then: Expects readiness to fall to 503 as the last successful cycle expires, exactly two check calls, and 200 liveness during the stall.

title: A stalled check in the emitted monitor blocks a second check callback
when: Runs a monitor that becomes ready, then holds its second check callback open.
then: Expects readiness to fall to 503 as the last successful cycle expires, exactly two check calls, and 200 liveness during the stall.

title: The assembled service keeps the probe routes public and the other routes protected
when: Builds and starts the generated service, then requests the two probe routes and one application route without and with an authorized header.
then: Expects 200 for each probe route, 401 for the unauthenticated application route, 204 for the authorized application route, and a clean shutdown on SIGTERM.

title: The emitted monitor refuses every invalid construction
when: Sends HEAD and POST to both probe paths, then builds a monitor with a nil context, a nil check, seventeen checks and a nil database.
then: Expects an empty body for HEAD, 405 with an Allow header for POST, and a refusal for every invalid construction.

title: The emitted probes answer HEAD with no body and refuse other methods with 405
when: Sends HEAD and POST to both probe paths, then builds a monitor with a nil context, a nil check, seventeen checks and a nil database.
then: Expects an empty body for HEAD, 405 with an Allow header for POST, and a refusal for every invalid construction.

title: The emitted HTTPS client keeps one verified origin
when: Runs the emitted client against a TLS test server for a wrong server name, escaping paths, a redirect, an over-large request and response, a deadline, a failed mutation, a closed client and a foreign origin, then its capacity, its credential files, its streams and its certificate pin.
then: Expects each unsafe case refused without reaching the service, the capacity limit refused instead of queued, only private credential modes accepted, every stream bound, and the pin checked beside the CA chain and the server name.

title: The emitted HTTPS client refuses a redirect and bounds both bodies
when: Runs the emitted client against a TLS test server for a wrong server name, escaping paths, a redirect, an over-large request and response, a deadline, a failed mutation, a closed client and a foreign origin, then its capacity, its credential files, its streams and its certificate pin.
then: Expects each unsafe case refused without reaching the service, the capacity limit refused instead of queued, only private credential modes accepted, every stream bound, and the pin checked beside the CA chain and the server name.

title: The emitted client refuses a call beyond its capacity
when: Holds the maximum number of requests open and starts one more.
then: Expects the extra call refused instead of queued, and capacity released when the held calls finish.

title: Closing the emitted client stops a live stream
when: Closes the client from inside a stream callback.
then: Expects the stream to end with an error promptly.

title: The emitted stream is bounded and cancellable
when: Streams a live frame then cancels, then streams over-large frames, over-large totals, a redirect, a foreign origin, an escaping path and a missing callback.
then: Expects the live frame delivered before cancellation and every unbounded or unsafe stream refused.

title: The emitted client reads only a private credential file
when: Reads a projected credential file at each permitted mode and at wider modes, then builds clients from invalid base URLs.
then: Expects only the four private modes accepted and every invalid base URL refused.

title: A certificate pin is copied and does not replace CA trust
when: Supplies an exact pin, a pin changed after construction, a different pin, no CA file, a wrong host name and an all-zero pin.
then: Expects the exact and copied pins accepted, the other cases refused without reaching the service, and the all-zero pin refused at construction.

title: The emitted client returns no data when the caller cancels during the response read
when: Cancels the caller's context from inside the response body read.
then: Expects an error with no status and no body, a closed response body and a released request permit.

title: The emitted endpoint verifies before it decodes
when: Sends valid, malformed, aliased, duplicated, over-long and unauthenticated bodies, then empty-status endpoints, dynamic replies, required members, a cancelled body read and a preparation callback.
then: Expects no domain call for a refused request, no-store on every answer, no private error text, empty answers without a body or content type, and the preparation callback run once between decoding and the domain call.

title: The emitted endpoint caches no response
when: Sends valid, malformed, aliased, duplicated, over-long and unauthenticated bodies, then empty-status endpoints, dynamic replies, required members, a cancelled body read and a preparation callback.
then: Expects no domain call for a refused request, no-store on every answer, no private error text, empty answers without a body or content type, and the preparation callback run once between decoding and the domain call.

title: The emitted endpoint reads one strict JSON object
when: Sends valid, malformed, aliased, duplicated, over-long and unauthenticated bodies, then empty-status endpoints, dynamic replies, required members, a cancelled body read and a preparation callback.
then: Expects no domain call for a refused request, no-store on every answer, no private error text, empty answers without a body or content type, and the preparation callback run once between decoding and the domain call.

title: A required member must be present but may be a zero value
when: Decodes bodies with zero values, explicit nulls, absent members, an empty nested object, an unknown tag value and untagged fields.
then: Expects zero values accepted, every absent or null required member refused, an unknown tag value reported as a configuration error, and untagged fields unchanged.

title: An emitted empty-status endpoint writes no body
when: Builds endpoints for status 202, 204 and 205 over a real connection and sends verified, denied and unauthenticated requests.
then: Expects no body and no content type, no-store on every answer, the domain not reached for an unauthenticated request, and construction refused for a body response type at 204 and 205.

title: An emitted dynamic reply fails closed on a wrong status and body pair
when: Returns each combination of status and body from a reply endpoint.
then: Expects 202 and 200 with a body, 204 and 205 without one, and a 500 answer for every other combination.

title: An emitted preparation callback runs once, in order, under the deadline
when: Sends a bad token, an undecodable request, a failing callback and a valid request, then builds endpoints with a nil callback and with two callbacks.
then: Expects the callback skipped for a token or decoding failure, run once with the verified identity and the request deadline otherwise, its failure kept apart from an authentication failure, and both invalid configurations refused.

title: A cancelled request stops the emitted body read
when: Cancels the request context while the endpoint reads a partial body from a pipe.
then: Expects the handler to return promptly with status 503.

title: A cancelled socket request stops the emitted body read
when: Cancels the server context while the endpoint reads a partial body from a real socket.
then: Expects status 503 on that connection.

title: The emitted endpoint keeps private error text private
when: Sends valid, malformed, aliased, duplicated, over-long and unauthenticated bodies, then empty-status endpoints, dynamic replies, required members, a cancelled body read and a preparation callback.
then: Expects no domain call for a refused request, no-store on every answer, no private error text, empty answers without a body or content type, and the preparation callback run once between decoding and the domain call.

title: The emitted order parser accepts only declared fields
when: Parses a valid two-entry order, then an unknown name, an injected statement, extra words, a trailing comma, a duplicate name, two aliases of one column and over-long input.
then: Expects the valid order mapped to its columns and directions and every other input refused.

title: The emitted projector keeps the envelope, checks its selectors and bounds every value
when: Projects a list with exact large integers, nested objects, object arrays, nulls and absent members, then invalid selectors, malformed responses, schema bounds, a schema changed after construction, concurrent calls and an absent selection.
then: Expects the envelope, the order and the exact values kept, undeclared data never exposed, each invalid case refused with the right contract error, and the normal path kept when the caller selects nothing.

title: The emitted projector checks a selector without reading data
when: Parses unknown paths, over-deep paths, invalid wildcards, empty terms, duplicates, wrong case, over-long input and control bytes, then overlapping parent and child paths.
then: Expects every invalid selector refused with the request error, and an overlapping selection giving the same result in any order.

title: The emitted projector refuses a malformed list response
when: Projects null, arrays, missing item arrays, non-object items, duplicate members, bad Unicode, trailing values, over-long arrays and an over-large encoded value.
then: Expects the projection error for each one and for a zero selection.

title: The emitted projector bounds data the caller did not select
when: Projects one selected field from items that exceed the member, element and depth limits in their unselected parts.
then: Expects the projection error in each case.

title: The emitted projector copies its schema and is safe to share
when: Builds projectors from invalid, cyclic and over-wide schemas, then widens a schema after construction, then projects from many goroutines.
then: Expects each invalid schema refused, the later change ignored, and no undeclared data exposed under concurrent use.

title: An unselected list keeps the normal response path
when: Calls the optional projector with no selection, with a selection, with a zero selection and with an invalid item field name.
then: Expects the original value returned unchanged and unencoded for no selection, the projected bytes for a selection, and the projection error for the two invalid cases.

title: The emitted scalar response mappings own their values

notes: Proved by TestGeneratedHTTPTLS; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A TLS connection gets the same request limits as a plaintext one
given: A service declaration with the http-application component and one endpoint, compiled and started in process twice: once with TLS (STEGO_HTTP_REQUIRE_TLS 1 and a test key pair) and once in plaintext.

title: A managed-client attribute key or client_id placeholder outside its form is refused before generation
when: Gives the keycloak-provider generator one managed gateway kind at a time with an attribute key that closes the Go string and adds code, a key with an upper-case letter, a key with a newline, a key of 112 characters, a key that starts with a dot, a client_id placeholder that holds Go code, a client_id placeholder that is not a declared id, a client_id with a brace outside a placeholder, and the client_id placeholders {panic(1)}, {string(rune(65))}, { gateway }, {} and {gateway[:0]}; then a key of 111 characters in the form and a client_id with a literal after its placeholder.
then: Expects the context check and generation to refuse each of the first thirteen with no file, and to accept the last one, whose client name keeps the literal after the placeholder.
notes: Level: unit. Finding 3 of the baseline security review of 2026-11-11: a key must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,110}$, so with the stego.owner. prefix it stays within the Keycloak attribute name limit, and each placeholder of client_id becomes a Go identifier, so it must be a declared id.

title: The emitted identity helpers write each attribute key as a quoted Go string

notes: Level: unit. The declaration check of ST-SUP-RC13-OC18-T02 refuses such a key; this test shows that the template quotes each key also when a check misses one (finding 3 of the baseline security review of 2026-11-11).

title: The emitted audience binding accepts a stored name for the legacy form only

title: A failed search from the emitted provider is not repeated or widened

then: Expects an error in each case, ErrResponse for the three invalid bodies, exactly one read, and no fall back to another query.

title: The emitted provider refuses an ambiguous provider response with ErrResponse

then: Expects ErrResponse in each case and no API request.

title: The emitted provider checks identifiers and pages before any request and stays in its realm
when: Looks up, pages and inspects clients, then reads seven unsafe identifiers and four invalid pages.

title: The emitted provider does not treat a record with no explicit state as disabled

title: Credential rotation and an unauthorized answer clear the emitted provider token cache

then: Expects the rotated secret used for the next grant, the unauthorized read failed without the provider body and without a replay, and a new grant for the later read.

title: Close and cancellation release every caller of the emitted provider
when: Holds the first authentication open, then calls with a canceled context, then with a short deadline, then closes the provider.
then: Expects the canceled caller released with context.Canceled, the waiting caller released with context.DeadlineExceeded, the first call canceled by Close, and ErrClosed for later work.

title: A span from the emitted provider keeps the caller trace and holds no request data

then: Expects the caller trace kept with a new span ID, no baggage or trace state sent, client spans with the response status, and no client name, provider ID, server URL or credential in the attributes.

title: The emitted lifecycle saves a prepared closure without a provider call
when: Prepares closure for a known provider ID with current and with legacy ownership, repeats it after a restart, then prepares with another ID and reconciles.

notes: Proved by TestServiceAccountLifecyclePrepareClosure; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted lifecycle closes a current-ownership client found by its saved ID
when: Closes a client that the provider holds under current ownership while the application also declares legacy keys, directly and after a prepared closure.
then: Expects the provider calls delete, inspect, delete only, the journal bound to the saved ID with closure kept, a repeat that changes nothing, a late client deleted, and reconcile refused with ErrClientClosed.
notes: Proved by TestServiceAccountLifecycleObservedClosure; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted lifecycle refuses closure of a foreign or unconfirmed client
when: Closes with an inspected client that differs in ID or name, holds a foreign or mixed ownership value or an undeclared reserved key, fails to read, or changes after the read.
then: Expects the closure refused, the provider client kept, the closure intent and ID kept, no unconfirmed binding saved, and no discovery or access call.
notes: Proved by TestServiceAccountLifecycleObservedClosureRejectsForeignOwnership; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A rejected or lost save stops the emitted closure until a retry

then: Expects the closure refused with the client kept and the intent saved, and a retry after the save works that deletes the client.
notes: Proved by TestServiceAccountLifecycleObservedClosureSaveFailure; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A rejected write is not retried

title: A computed patch is not retried after a conflict

title: A watch reconnect reads the replaced token file

then: The reconnect uses the replaced token.

title: A replaced token file takes effect on the next request
when: The client makes a request, the test writes a new token to the same file, and the client makes another request.
then: The server sees the new bearer token without a client restart.

title: Discovery reads the token file again for each call
when: The requirement check passes once, then the token file is replaced and the server stops reporting the resource, and the check runs again.
then: The second call uses the new bearer token.

title: The emitted client reads a rotated projected token on a live cluster
when: Runs inside a dedicated cluster Job whose projected service account token rotates, and makes requests across a rotation.
then: Expects each request to carry the token current at that moment.
notes: Gated: the test skips unless STEGO_KUBERNETES_LIVE_ROTATION is 1, because it needs a dedicated cluster Job with a projected token. It gives no proof on a workstation or in an ordinary CI job. Lathe counts a product test as proof as it stands, so this proof is real only where that Job runs.

title: A registry credential file that other users can read is refused

then: The public file is refused and reaches no write.

title: A world-readable token file is refused
when: The test changes the token file mode to 0644, and the client makes a request.
then: The request after the mode change fails before it reaches the server.

title: A foreign, unidentified, conflicted or denied resource is never updated or deleted

then: Every call fails, the foreign and unidentified resources receive no write at all, and each invalid desired object and the empty owner are refused before any request.

title: A computed patch is refused when the ownership labels do not match
when: PatchOwned sends a change computed from an earlier read against a server that answers 409, then runs with five patches that hold a system field or no field, two wrong observed paths, and foreign owner labels.
then: The call with foreign owner labels is refused before any further request.

title: A patch and a delete of an owned resource carry its observed UID and version
when: The generated client calls Ensure twice with the same desired Widget, then changes it, then calls DeleteOwned twice against a fake API server.
then: The patch and the delete carry the observed UID and resource version.

title: A computed patch carries the preconditions of its original observation
when: PatchOwned sends a change computed from an earlier read against a server that answers 409, then runs with five patches that hold a system field or no field, two wrong observed paths, and foreign owner labels.
then: The one PATCH carries the original UID and resource version.

title: A converged owned resource gets no second write
when: The generated client calls Ensure twice with the same desired Widget, then changes it, then calls DeleteOwned twice against a fake API server.
then: The second Ensure sends no write.

title: Deletion of an owned resource reports absence only after it is gone
when: The generated client calls Ensure twice with the same desired Widget, then changes it, then calls DeleteOwned twice against a fake API server.
then: The first DeleteOwned reports false while the deletion is pending, and the second reports true.

title: Convergence does not change the caller's desired object
when: The generated client calls Ensure twice with the same desired Widget, then changes it, then calls DeleteOwned twice against a fake API server.
then: The caller's desired object is unchanged.

title: A computed patch does not change the caller's observation or changes
when: PatchOwned sends a change computed from an earlier read against a server that answers 409, then runs with five patches that hold a system field or no field, two wrong observed paths, and foreign owner labels.
then: The caller's two input objects are unchanged.

title: A large integer keeps its exact value and a response that is not one JSON object is refused
when: The server returns the integer 9007199254740993, then null, then an array, then two objects in one body.
then: The decoded value keeps its exact text and matches the exact int64 but not the neighbouring value, and each of the three other bodies returns an error.

title: A rejected write reports only status metadata
when: The generated client sends a POST, a PUT and a PATCH with a caller query that already selects weaker validation, then sends two writes with a malformed query.
then: The rejected write returns only the method and the status.

title: A rate-limited response reports only status metadata and no response body
when: The server answers 429 with a Retry-After header of 120 and a private body.
then: The error holds only the method, the status 429 and a two-minute delay.

title: The public failure summary reports only a known method and a valid status
when: The summary reads a plain error that holds a private value, an API error with an unknown method, an API error with an out-of-range status, a wrapped API error, and nil.
then: The first three return the fixed text, the wrapped error keeps only its method and status, and nil returns an empty string.

title: A parsed retry delay is limited to one hour
when: The delay parser reads a negative value, an invalid value, 999999 seconds, one second and an HTTP date.
then: The parser returns zero for the invalid inputs and caps the delay at one hour.

title: Observation sends RESET before each list and REPLACE after the complete snapshot
when: A fake API server returns a two-page list, one watch event, a bookmark, an expired-history error, and a later list and delete, while the token file changes during observation.
then: The callback receives RESET, REPLACE, MODIFIED, RESET, REPLACE and DELETED in that order.

title: An inconsistent or repeated list snapshot never becomes a baseline
when: One observation cycle runs against a server that changes the list resource version between pages, repeats an object UID, or repeats a cursor.
then: Each case returns an error, and no REPLACE reaches the consumer.

title: The watch uses the snapshot cursor without list paging
when: A fake API server returns a two-page list, one watch event, a bookmark, an expired-history error, and a later list and delete, while the token file changes during observation.
then: Each list page is bounded and keeps its cursor, and the watch uses the snapshot version without paging options.

title: Expired watch history starts a new list
when: A fake API server returns a two-page list, one watch event, a bookmark, an expired-history error, and a later list and delete, while the token file changes during observation.
then: The expired-history error starts a new list, and the next watch uses the version of that list.

title: A denied list or watch stops observation
when: One observation cycle runs against a server that denies the list, or denies only the watch.
then: Both denial cases return ErrWatchAccess, and no REPLACE reaches the consumer except in the watch-denied case where the list was complete.

title: An empty page keeps its objects and an oversized snapshot is stopped before it becomes a baseline
when: The server returns a first empty page and then one object, or an endless run of cursors, or an endless run of full 100-object pages.
then: The empty-page case still delivers the one object in its REPLACE, the two endless cases return an error with no REPLACE and no retained cursor, and the page count stays inside the page bound.

title: An invalid collection path makes no request and a consumer error stops observation
when: Observe runs with an absolute URL, a dot-dot path, a percent-encoded dot-dot path, a path that carries a query, and a path with an empty segment, then with a consumer that returns an error.
then: No invalid path reaches the server, and the consumer's own error comes back from Observe.

title: API discovery reads one bounded response and fails closed on any missing or changed requirement
when: The requirement check runs for a core path, a grouped path, and eleven answers that are missing, partial, of the wrong group version, kind or namespace scope, short of a verb, duplicated, malformed, denied or unavailable.
then: Each run makes exactly one request, the valid and core answers pass, the HTTP failures keep their status metadata, and every other answer returns ErrDiscovery.

title: An invalid group version or resource requirement is refused before any request
when: The requirement check runs with seven invalid group versions and seven invalid requirement sets, including a subresource name, a missing verb list, a repeated verb, an unknown verb and 33 entries.
then: Every call returns ErrDiscovery and the fake server records no request.

title: Discovery reads the API again for each call, so removed support is not cached
when: The requirement check passes once, then the token file is replaced and the server stops reporting the resource, and the check runs again.
then: The second call returns ErrDiscovery instead of the earlier success.

title: Deployment availability requires a complete current rollout
when: The availability check reads an available Deployment and then eleven pending variants, including exact int64 generations.
then: The available Deployment passes, and each pending variant reports false without an error.

title: A paused or deleting Deployment is not available
when: The availability check reads a paused Deployment and a deleting Deployment.
then: Each one reports false without an error.

title: A malformed Deployment observation is an error
when: The availability check reads twelve foreign or malformed variants of an available Deployment, and three out-of-range replica requirements.
then: Each foreign or malformed variant returns ErrResourceObservation, and each out-of-range replica requirement is refused.

notes: Level: unit. Not automated yet: no test names this ID yet. Planned file internal/generator/kubernetesclient/testdata/observation_test.go. A certificate with revocation addresses catches a check that fetches them.

then: The valid Routes pass, and each wrong Route or host requirement returns ErrResourceObservation.

when: The admission check reads Routes with path routing, a wildcard policy, an alternate backend, a zero weight, TLS termination at the router, plain HTTP, and router TLS data.
then: Each Route returns ErrResourceObservation.

title: Missing Route admission is pending without an error

then: The helper returns false without an error and does not call the probe.

title: Missing Route admission stays pending and is not an error

then: The probe runs once and only after admission passes, a failed probe stops the helper before a second read, and a Route that is removed or denied on the read after the probe returns false.

title: Route exposure fails when the Route identity changes around the probe

then: The helper returns false without an error.

title: Route exposure refuses a stored Route whose namespace differs
when: The Route helper runs against a fake API server that returns the Route with a foreign namespace.
then: The helper returns false and does not call the probe.

then: Each variant returns ErrResourceObservation with no returned data.

then: Every invalid variant returns ErrResourceObservation with no extra text and no returned data.

title: Client TLS Secret verification hides its reasons and holds its data limits
when: The client verifier reads every invalid Secret variant, including an oversized certificate, an oversized key and a chain longer than sixteen certificates.
then: Every invalid variant returns ErrResourceObservation with no extra text and no returned data.

title: Client TLS Secret verification refuses a server-only certificate

then: The verifier returns ErrResourceObservation.

when: The digest is computed for nineteen invalid sets covering a foreign owner, a missing UID or version, a wrong namespace, name, kind, API version or type, a deleting Secret, an invalid data key or value, non-canonical base64, the entry and total size bounds, and duplicate names, then for an invalid namespace, an empty set, a short set and a missing owner.

title: Registry credential JSON is accepted only as auths data for the exact selected registries

title: Registry credentials are read again from the private file on every call

title: The controller Deployment carries the lease release grace period
given: A service declaration with the kubernetes-service component and the modes api, worker and controller (one controller replica), generated into a temporary folder, with the generated renderer run.

Flush before release is ST-SUP-RP09-LC06 (decision on ST-SUP-Q37). The statement names no readiness probe and no upper bound for controller; the probe and the lease TTL bound of the first draft were removed. Slow the checkpoint write with a lock held by the test, so that a grace period too short for the release is caught. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it.

when: Generates the service with the outbox component and the runtime outbox, and applies every emitted migration to PostgreSQL from pgtest.
then: Expects the migrations to apply once with no duplicate table error, and stego_outbox.messages to have the runtime outbox's columns, policies and relay functions.
notes: Level: integration. internal/generator/outbox/runtime_test.go (TestGeneratedRuntimeOutbox) generates the outbox, audit-log and idempotency components of the service orders with gen.Context.RuntimeData into a temporary module, builds it against the runtime module of this repository with the Go SDK of STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO, and runs this test there against the PostgreSQL server of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, a local container of the pgtest image (ST-STD-LOCAL). Each test makes its own database, owned by an owner role that is a member of the outbox relay role of the test service WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE, and applies the emitted migrations as that owner; the owner reads the messages of every tenant only as that role, with SET ROLE. The test applies, each once and as the owner, the key table of the idempotency component, the audit tables of the audit-log component and the emitted outbox Migration, and reads information_schema.columns, pg_policies and pg_proc. TestRuntimeOutput in internal/generator/outbox/runtime_test.go also checks that no emitted file of the three components creates the queue table or the schema stego_outbox, that the outbox emits only internal/outbox/outbox.go on github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime/outbox, and that a service with no entity, no command and no query gets no file. Not covered yet: the tables of the entity Order and their row-level security, which the PostgreSQL adapter and the tenancy component emit for the GORM migration ledger, and spicedb-authz and its SpiceDB container, which has no component in the registry yet (ST-SUP-RC29). The owner of the test holds no CREATEROLE: the runtime migration makes the relay role only when it is missing.

title: An upgraded database gets the runtime queue table and keeps the former messages
given: The service of ST-SUP-RC18-OC30-T01 on a database where the migration of the former outbox component ran: stego_outbox.messages with no tenant_id, no state and no row-level security.
when: Applies the emitted outbox migration while the former table holds one message; then empties the former table and applies it again; then enqueues one message of tenant t1 and applies it a third time.
then: Expects the first run refused with an error that names the former messages and the former table and its message unchanged; the second run to give the runtime queue table with its columns, policies and relay functions; and the third run to succeed and keep the message.
notes: Level: integration. internal/generator/outbox/runtime_test.go (TestGeneratedRuntimeOutbox) generates the outbox, audit-log and idempotency components of the service orders with gen.Context.RuntimeData into a temporary module, builds it against the runtime module of this repository with the Go SDK of STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO, and runs this test there against the PostgreSQL server of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, a local container of the pgtest image (ST-STD-LOCAL). Each test makes its own database, owned by an owner role that is a member of the outbox relay role of the test service WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE, and applies the emitted migrations as that owner; the owner reads the messages of every tenant only as that role, with SET ROLE. The former migration is internal/generator/outbox/testdata/former.sql, the migration that the former outbox component emitted; the outer test copies it into the module. Decision of this change: the step before the runtime migration drops an empty former table and stops on one that holds messages, because those messages have no tenant and only the former worker can deliver them.

title: The roles get only the grants of the runtime migration and the tenant wall
given: The service of ST-SUP-RC18-OC30-T01 with every emitted migration applied, a runtime role and a worker role.
when: Reads the table, column and function privileges of the two roles on stego_outbox.messages, its row-level security and its order index; enqueues one message of t1 and one of t2 as the runtime role; then reads and updates the messages in a transaction of t1.
then: Expects SELECT and the INSERT of the enqueue columns only, no UPDATE, no DELETE and no INSERT of state or attempts for both roles, EXECUTE on claim for the worker role only, row-level security enabled and forced, tenant_id first in the order index, only the message of t1 visible, and the update refused. Expects the outbox wiring to give the database access contract no object.
notes: Level: integration. internal/generator/outbox/runtime_test.go (TestGeneratedRuntimeOutbox) generates the outbox, audit-log and idempotency components of the service orders with gen.Context.RuntimeData into a temporary module, builds it against the runtime module of this repository with the Go SDK of STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO, and runs this test there against the PostgreSQL server of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, a local container of the pgtest image (ST-STD-LOCAL). Each test makes its own database, owned by an owner role that is a member of the outbox relay role of the test service WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE, and applies the emitted migrations as that owner; the owner reads the messages of every tenant only as that role, with SET ROLE. TestRuntimeOutput in internal/generator/outbox/runtime_test.go checks the wiring: the former component granted SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE through the database access contract, and the runtime migration now grants the roles itself.

title: A message reaches the outside system through the destination that the wiring registers

when: Writes one audit event of t1 through the audit writer on the emitted AuditQueue in a transaction of t1, builds the worker with the emitted NewWorker once with no audit-sink port and once with the recording sink, and runs it as the worker role.
then: Expects the destination list audit-sink, the payload limit of audit-sink at audit.MaxSinkMessage and of another destination at outbox.MaxPayloadBytes, the worker with no port refused naming the port, audit-sink registered as idempotent and must land, the event in the sink once with tenant t1, and the message done.
notes: Level: integration. internal/generator/outbox/runtime_test.go (TestGeneratedRuntimeOutbox) generates the outbox, audit-log and idempotency components of the service orders with gen.Context.RuntimeData into a temporary module, builds it against the runtime module of this repository with the Go SDK of STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO, and runs this test there against the PostgreSQL server of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, a local container of the pgtest image (ST-STD-LOCAL). title: A writer of the former outbox that races the drop keeps its message
given: The service of ST-SUP-RC18-OC30-T01 on a database where the migration of the former outbox component ran and its queue table is empty, and a writer of the former release that has inserted one message and has not committed.
when: Starts the emitted outbox migration, waits until it waits for a lock on the former table, and then commits the writer.
then: Expects the migration to stop with the refusal that the former table holds messages, and the former table to keep the message of the writer.
notes: Level: integration, against PostgreSQL from pgtest, through the generated module of TestGeneratedRuntimeOutbox. Proved by TestMigrations, subtest ST-SUP-RC18-OC30-T07. formerTable locks stego_outbox.messages in ACCESS EXCLUSIVE mode in the transaction of the migration before it checks for messages. Mutation caught: formerTable without the LOCK TABLE (the migration does not see the uncommitted message, drops the table after the commit, and passes with the message lost).

title: With kafka-producer, NewWorker registers the Kafka destination of the runtime with its settings and the log provider of the worker
given: The service of ST-SUP-RC18-OC30-T01 with the audit-log component, once with the kafka-producer component and once without it.
when: Generates the outbox wiring of each, and builds the wiring with kafka-producer with go vet against the runtime module.
then: Expects the wiring with kafka-producer to import kafkaoutbox, to name the destinations audit-sink and kafka, to read kafkaoutbox.ReadSettings, to call kafkaoutbox.New(settings, config.Logger) and to register its Registration, with no grant and no module requirement; and the wiring without kafka-producer to name no Kafka.

TestGeneratedRuntimeOutbox builds the wiring with kafka-producer in the package internal/eventsoutbox of the generated module. title: The generated worker sends to Kafka with the settings of the process, and does not start without them or with no topic
given: The rest-crud service wiring-shop of internal/compiler/testdata/runtime_wiring/project/service.yaml with the mixin event-publisher, generated with stego apply, built, and run against PostgreSQL, SpiceDB and a local Kafka broker.
when: Runs the binary in the worker mode with the environment of the service, no broker setting and the topic; then in the worker mode with the brokers and no STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC and no STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC_FILE; then runs the service with all modes and the settings STEGO_KAFKA_BROKERS, STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC and STEGO_KAFKA_INSECURE_LOOPBACK=1, and creates an order.
then: Expects the run with no broker setting to exit with the failure record of the stage service.run and the task stego-runtime[0]; the run with no topic to exit with the failure record of the stage service.start.setting.kafka-producer.STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC, with no task stego-runtime[0]; and the change event of the create done in the outbox of the service with the settings.
notes: Level: system. Proved by the subtest of this ID in the check of the generated service, which internal/compiler/runtime_wiring_test.go (TestRuntimeWiring) builds with the pinned Go and runs. The service wiring-shop binds the mixin event-publisher. Local stand-ins (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, a local SpiceDB container, and the Kafka broker of kafkatest (registry/runtime/kafkatest), a local container without privilege (apache/kafka:4.1.1 at a pinned digest, 512 MiB, one CPU) that the check starts once and removes, reached through a proxy of kafkatest on 127.0.0.1, in the insecure loopback mode of the Kafka destination, for tests only. The failure record holds no error text (ST-SUP-RP14-LC05). Walkthrough 7, B7 (run 6 K7): with no topic the worker mode started and sent each message to the topic of its event type, which the topic need does not state, so every delivery was refused for ever; the generated start now refuses it at the stage of the topic setting. Mutation caught: NewWorker that does not register the destination (the event of the create is never done).

title: The generated service links no test support of the runtime library

title: A body with two bad members gets a validation problem with one entry for each
when: Generates the rest-api package of the runtime data path with request validation openapi-schema into a module, and runs a test in the generated package that posts to the todos route a body whose title is a number and whose done is a string.
then: Expects 400 with the handler not called, and validation_errors with one entry for done and one for title.
notes: Developer walkthrough of 2026-11-13, step 13 (F3): the emitted middleware listed only the first bad member. It now validates with MultiError and walks nested MultiErrors. Mutations caught: no MultiError option (only done listed); no walk of the MultiError (one entry with no field).

title: A validation problem lists at most 50 failed members and one entry that counts the rest
when: Generates the rest-api package of the runtime data path with request validation openapi-schema into a module, and runs a test in the generated package that gives parseValidationErrors a nested MultiError of 50, 51 and 120 schema failures.
then: Expects 50 entries for 50 failures with no count entry; and for 51 and 120 failures, 50 entries and one last entry that says 1 or 70 more failures not listed. Expects MaxValidationErrors to be 50.
notes: Security review low S2 of #268 (OWASP API4, CWE-770): an array schema let a 1 MiB body make 524278 entries. Generated request schemas hold no arrays today. Mutations caught: no cap; no count entry.

title: No validation entry quotes a value of the request
when: Generates the rest-api package as in ST-SUP-RC20-OC05-T04, and runs a test in the generated package that posts six bad bodies to the todos route, each with a marked value (wrong types, a cut string, a bad token, no JSON), and gives parseValidationErrors a schema error with no reason and parse errors that hold a marked value.
then: Expects 400 for each body and no marked value in any problem body or entry.
notes: Security review low S2 of #268. The text of a schema error with no reason and of a parse error quotes the value, so the entries use the reason or a fixed message. Mutations caught: the schema error text, the parse error text, the error text as the last fallback.

title: A create or a PUT that leaves out a required member gets a validation problem that names it
when: Generates the rest-api package of the runtime data path with request validation openapi-schema into a module, and runs a test in the generated package that sends to the todos routes a POST and a PUT whose body is {} or {"done":true}, which leave out the required member title, and then a POST and a PUT that hold title.
then: Expects each body with no title to get 400 with the handler not called and validation_errors with one entry whose field is title and whose message names title, and each body with title to reach the handler.
notes: The security review of #328 saw that the generated create decode (decode<Collection>) has no required-member check, so a body with no title would store "". This test proves that the validation middleware refuses such a body before the decode: the request schema of a create and of a PUT lists each required member, and kin-openapi refuses a missing member with a schema error whose pointer is the member. TestCrudService serves its handlers with no middleware, so its checks do not show this. then: Expects a valid OpenAPI 3.0 document with the operation closeTodo marked as a command, the required Idempotency-Key header and path parameter, a body with no path member and each member in its protobuf JSON form, the int64 as a string, the 409 that names the refusal, the get query with its path parameter, the list query with cursor, limit and a page of items and next; the request validation to pass over a command body; and OpenAPIDocument to give the same document; the request validation skips the check of a body only when the marker is true, never when it is only present (security review of PR #454, INFO).
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestCommandAndQueryRoutes. Real use: walkthrough-14 patients with both clients, in the core31 proof folder. Mutation caught (fu/standing-21): the skip on a marker that is present (!= nil) in place of true.

title: A member that the proto marks debug_redact is x-sensitive, a password string, and writeOnly in a request body
given: A todo service with the command close-todo whose request message has the members pin and codes (a list) marked debug_redact, a nested message Note with the member token marked, and plain members, and whose response message has the member api_key marked.
when: Gives the OpenAPI document of the rest-api component.
then: Expects a valid OpenAPI 3.0 document; x-sensitive, the format password and writeOnly on pin and on token of the nested message; x-sensitive and writeOnly with no format on the list codes; x-sensitive and the format password and no writeOnly on apiKey of the response; and none of the marks on reason, text and todoId.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestCommandSecretMembers. Security review of PR #454, L2; decision ST-SUP-Q192 (a). Mutations caught (fu/standing-24): no writeOnlySecrets on the body; no x-sensitive on a marked member; no format password.

title: A response that holds a debug_redact member deeper than the schema follows is x-sensitive at its root
given: The todo service of ST-SUP-RC20-OC54-T01 with three proto files: a response whose member api_key, marked debug_redact, is at depth 9 of nested messages; a response with a marked member at depth 1; and a response with no marked member.
when: Gives the OpenAPI document of the rest-api component for each.
then: Expects a valid OpenAPI document each time, and x-sensitive at the root of the response schema for the first two and not for the third.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestCommandResponseSecretRoot. Security review of PR #460, L1: the schema follows 8 levels, so a deeper secret had no mark and the CLI did not make the command Sensitive. Mutation caught (fu/standing-25): no root mark.

title: A path parameter that the proto marks debug_redact is refused
given: The todo service with the command close-todo at POST /todos/{todo_id}/state:close.
when: Gives the OpenAPI document with the request member todo_id marked debug_redact, and with it plain.
then: Expects the marked path parameter refused with an error that names it and says that a secret member cannot be a path parameter, and the plain one accepted.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestCommandSecretPathParameter. Security review of PR #460, L2: a path parameter goes in the URL, the access logs and a CLI flag. Mutation caught (fu/standing-25): no refusal.

title: The members token and pin of verify-order, which the fixture proto marks debug_redact, are secrets in the generated service
given: The service of testdata/runtime_wiring/project, whose proto marks the members token and pin of VerifyOrderRequest debug_redact; TestRuntimeWiring sends verify-order with them to the running service.
when: Applies the service with stego and reads the generated OpenAPI document and runtime wiring.
then: Expects token and pin of the verify-order body with x-sensitive, writeOnly and the format password, orderId with no mark, and a runtime wiring that reads the key ring.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestRuntimeDataPath. Security review of PR #460, I3: an example of debug_redact from the proto to the running service. Mutation caught (fu/standing-25): pin with no mark in the fixture proto.

title: A service of the rpc-service archetype, with no rest-api, refuses a path parameter that the proto marks debug_redact
given: The service of testdata/runtime_grpc/project on the rpc-service archetype, whose components hold command and no rest-api, with the command add-note at POST /orders/{orderId}/notes.
when: Plans the service with stego, then plans it again with the member order_id of AddNoteRequest marked debug_redact.
then: Expects the first plan accepted, and the second refused with an error that names orderId and says that a secret member cannot be a path parameter, with no output folder.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestGRPCSecretPathParameter. Security review of PR #462, L2: the check of rest-api 4.23.0 did not hold for the command routes that the command component mounts with no rest-api. Mutation caught (fu/standing-25): no refusal in planRoute.

title: A response that holds google.protobuf.Any, Struct, Value or ListValue at any depth is x-stego-opaque at its root, and is not x-sensitive
given: The todo service of ST-SUP-RC20-OC53-T01 whose command response holds, in a nested message, one of: a Struct, a list of Any, a map of Value, a ListValue, a Timestamp only, or plain members only.
when: Generates the OpenAPI document of the rest-api component for each case and reads it with kin-openapi.
then: Expects a valid document; x-stego-opaque true at the root of the response for the Struct, the list of Any, the map of Value and the ListValue, and no mark for the Timestamp and the plain members; and in no case x-sensitive, so the mark asks no key ring.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestCommandOpaqueResponse. Decision ST-SUP-Q194 (a), security review of PR #462. Mutations caught (fu/standing-26): no mark on the root; no walk of the nested members.

title: A create, an update and an upsert refuse a member that they do not take, also in another letter case, store nothing, and take a read row sent back
given: The generated test service on PostgreSQL and SpiceDB, with the collection tickets (create, update and upsert by code), a ticket c1 with the title first, and the collection red-events whose implicit field source is red.
when: Sends a create, an update of c1, an upsert of a new code and an upsert of c1, each with one of the members Title, titel, tenant and CODE with a marked value; then sends back the read row of c1 with a new title as an update, an upsert of c1 and a create with kind Ticket and the right names, and a create of a red event with the source blue.
then: Expects each write with a wrong member to answer 400 with a problem that names the member and does not hold the value, only the first ticket stored and its title first; the read row sent back to answer 200 with the new title, the upsert 200 and the create 201; and the red event with the source blue to answer 400 that names source, with no event row.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestCrud of the generated service, which TestCrudService runs (crudCheckIDs) on PostgreSQL given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN and a local SpiceDB container, unprivileged (ST-STD-LOCAL). Decision ST-SUP-Q195. Mutations caught: no member check in the decode of a create, an update or an upsert (each write with a wrong member answered 2xx); no implicit check (the red event with the source blue answered 201).

title: The OpenAPI document closes the create and update requests, and the request check and the decode refuse a member that they do not take
given: The test declaration of the rest-api generator in the envelope format, with the collection tickets over Ticket (create, update, patch and upsert, with kept, secret and client-set fields) and the collection red-events whose implicit field source is red.
when: Generates the service, reads TicketCreateRequest and TicketUpdateRequest, runs the request check of the service on a create, an update and an upsert body with the member Title, titel or tenant_id, and with kind, id and a null href, and reads the decode of tickets and of red-events.
then: Expects each request schema to hold only the fields of Ticket, kind with the one value Ticket, id and href, with additionalProperties false, id and href as optional x-output-only members and state as an optional x-kept member; the check to refuse each wrong member by name and to take kind, id and the null href; the decode of red-events to refuse a member given twice, then each member that is not kind, id, href or a field, and a source other than red, then to remove the server-set members before it decodes the body, and to refuse a decoded source other than red; and the decode of the patch of tickets to refuse a member given twice before its member check.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestStrictBodies. Decision ST-SUP-Q195. Mutations caught: no additionalProperties false on the create request; an x-output-only member that is not nullable (a read row with href null was refused); no member check in the decode.

title: The Go client is made from a service document whose closed request schemas hold x-kept and x-output-only members
given: A service document as the rest-api component writes it for a create: WidgetCreateRequest with additionalProperties false, kind, an x-kept member and two x-output-only members with no type that take null.
when: Checks and generates the Go SDK from the document as the service document, then checks it again with the extension x-go-type in place of x-kept.
then: Expects the check and the generation to pass with files, and the document with x-go-type to be refused.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestServiceDocument. Decision ST-SUP-Q195: the input check of the SDKs took only x-sensitive and x-stego-command, so each document of a rest-api service with a closed request was refused. Mutation caught: x-kept and x-output-only not in the known extensions of internal/openapicontract (the generation was refused).

title: The TypeScript client is made from a document whose closed request schemas hold x-kept and x-output-only members
given: The sample document of the TypeScript SDK with RecordCreateRequest as the body of the create: additionalProperties false, kind, an x-kept member and an x-output-only member with no type that takes null.
when: Checks and generates the TypeScript SDK, then checks the document again with the extension x-other in place of x-output-only.
then: Expects the check and the generation to pass with the three files, and the document with x-other to be refused.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestStrictRequest. Decision ST-SUP-Q195. Mutation caught: x-kept and x-output-only not in the known extensions of internal/openapicontract (the check refused the document).

title: The CLI gives no flag for kind or for an x-kept or x-output-only member of a closed create request
given: The notes service document of the CLI tests with NoteCreateRequest closed, with kind, the x-kept member state, the x-output-only member created_by of type string and the x-output-only member id with no type.
when: Generates the CLI from the document and reads the apply definitions.
then: Expects the create fields of the apply resource Note to be only name and size, and no definition with the key kind, state, created_by or id.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestFactoryStrictRequest. Decision ST-SUP-Q195. Mutation caught: no skip of an x-output-only member in bodyFields (the definitions gave a flag to created_by).

title: The request check names an unknown member of a create, an update, an upsert and a patch in the field of its entry
given: The rest-crud test service of crudContext with request validation openapi-schema, built with its generated validation middleware.
when: Sends through the middleware a create of todos with the member Title, an update of a todo with titel, a patch of a todo with titel and an upsert of tickets with tenant_id, each with a marked value.
then: Expects each to answer 400 before the handler, with one validation entry whose field is the member and no marked value in the problem.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestValidationEveryField, which runs the check TestUnknownMember in the generated module. The walkthrough-16 proof of core35 found that kin-openapi names an unknown member of a closed schema only in the reason of its failure, so the entry had an empty field. Mutation caught: no member taken from the reason (the entry field was empty).

title: A write refuses a member given twice, cuts a long member name, and ignores a server-set member of another type
given: The generated test service on PostgreSQL and SpiceDB, with a ticket c1 with the title first, the collection red-events whose implicit field source is red, and the collection meetings whose noted_at the server sets.
when: Sends a create, an update (with the second title escaped as \u0074itle), an upsert and a patch of tickets that each give title twice, and a red event that gives source a value and then null; then a create with a member name of 300 bytes; then a create of a ticket with id 5 and href [1], and a meeting with noted_at 7.
then: Expects each body with a member given twice to answer 400 with a problem that names the member, says that the body gives it more than once and holds no value, and no row to change; the long name to be named by its first 128 bytes only; and the creates with server-set members of another JSON type to answer 201, the ticket with a new id.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestCrud of the generated service, which TestCrudService runs (crudCheckIDs) on PostgreSQL and a local SpiceDB container, unprivileged (ST-STD-LOCAL). Security review of PR #464: LOW (a duplicate member that ends in null passed the implicit check) and two INFO findings. Mutations caught: no duplicate check (the bodies with a member given twice got another answer); no cut of the name (the field held all 300 bytes); no removal of the server-set members before the decode (400 the body does not decode).

title: With no idempotency component, a create and a patch take the key, not required, and no other operation does
given: The rest-crud declaration of ST-SUP-RC30-OC01-T03 with the entity Todo and create, read, list, patch, update and delete, with no idempotency component in the service.
when: Reads the emitted OpenAPI document.
then: Expects the Idempotency-Key header parameter, not required, a 422 response and the header Idempotency-Kept on each response of the create and the patch, and no Idempotency-Key parameter and no Idempotency-Kept on any other operation.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestIdempotencyKeyHeader. Real use: the core37 lab proof on a running rest-crud with no idempotency setting (a create sent twice with one key was replayed, another body with the key was 422). Mutation check: with apply giving the operation back unchanged when there is no component, and with no 422 response, the test fails. With the header Idempotency-Kept written only by the idempotency component, the test fails too.

title: With no idempotency component, the create and patch handlers mark each answer to a request with a key Idempotency-Kept
given: The rest-crud declaration of ST-SUP-RC30-OC01-T03 with no idempotency component in the service.
when: Generates the handlers on the runtime data path.
then: Expects the create and the patch handler, and no other, each to set Idempotency-Kept: 1 right after the read of a key that the request gives.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestKeptKeyWithNoComponent. Real use: the core37 lab proof answers Idempotency-Kept: 1 to a create with a key with no idempotency setting. Mutation check: with the mark written only when the component is active, the test fails.

title: With no idempotency component, a refused key of a create or a patch takes the problem type under the problem base, as a command does
given: The rest-crud declaration of ST-SUP-RC30-OC01-T03 with no idempotency component in the service, with the problem base and then with none.
when: Generates the handlers on the runtime data path and reads the problem types of the key in runtime.go.
then: Expects, with the problem base, keyMissingType, keyInvalidType, keyBusyType and keyReusedType to be the base joined to idempotency-key-missing, idempotency-key-invalid, idempotency-key-in-progress and idempotency-key-reused, and the refusal of a key to take them; with no problem base, each to be about:blank.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestKeptKeyWithNoComponent. Walkthrough 19, W19-U3: a malformed Idempotency-Key on a collection create or patch of a service with no idempotency setting got 400 about:blank with the code <SVC>-VAL-001, while a command got idempotency-key-invalid. Real use: the core41 proof on the catalog service of walkthrough 19. Mutation check: with the problem base not used when the component is absent, the subtest fails.

title: The emitted SSO handler verifies the token before it maps any claim
when: Sends fourteen token cases through the handler, then requests each public path and each subpath, then calls Stop twice and repeats a valid request.
then: Expects 401 for a wrong issuer, a wrong audience, an absent expiry, an absent issuer, audience, subject or issue time, a future issue time, an expired token, a wrong signature, a wrong algorithm, a repeated header and an oversize token, 204 for the valid token only, a denial response with no token and both safety headers, 204 for each exact public path, 401 for each subpath, and 401 after Stop.

title: The emitted SSO handler denies a wrong issuer, a wrong audience and an absent expiry
when: Sends fourteen token cases through the handler, then requests each public path and each subpath, then calls Stop twice and repeats a valid request.
then: Expects 401 for a wrong issuer, a wrong audience, an absent expiry, an absent issuer, audience, subject or issue time, a future issue time, an expired token, a wrong signature, a wrong algorithm, a repeated header and an oversize token, 204 for the valid token only, a denial response with no token and both safety headers, 204 for each exact public path, 401 for each subpath, and 401 after Stop.

when: Sends fourteen token cases through the handler, then requests each public path and each subpath, then calls Stop twice and repeats a valid request.
then: Expects 401 for a wrong issuer, a wrong audience, an absent expiry, an absent issuer, audience, subject or issue time, a future issue time, an expired token, a wrong signature, a wrong algorithm, a repeated header and an oversize token, 204 for the valid token only, a denial response with no token and both safety headers, 204 for each exact public path, 401 for each subpath, and 401 after Stop.

title: A denial from the emitted SSO handler hides the token and sets no-store and WWW-Authenticate
when: Sends fourteen token cases through the handler, then requests each public path and each subpath, then calls Stop twice and repeats a valid request.
then: Expects 401 for a wrong issuer, a wrong audience, an absent expiry, an absent issuer, audience, subject or issue time, a future issue time, an expired token, a wrong signature, a wrong algorithm, a repeated header and an oversize token, 204 for the valid token only, a denial response with no token and both safety headers, 204 for each exact public path, 401 for each subpath, and 401 after Stop.

title: The emitted SSO handler fills each payload field from its declared claim order
when: Verifies a token in the SSO, OIDC and name-fallback claim shapes.
then: Expects the username, first name, last name, email, client and issuer from the declared claim order, the mapped username as UserID, an empty Role and the retained verified expiry.

then: Expects the username, first name, last name, email, client and issuer from the declared claim order, the mapped username as UserID, an empty Role and the retained verified expiry.

when: Verifies a token whose subject is caller and whose username is account.
then: Expects Identity.UserID to be caller, the issuer to be the verified issuer, and Identity.Username to be account.

title: The emitted SSO handler refuses to start without an issuer, an audience or a key
when: Starts the handler with no issuer, with no audience, with AUTH_ENABLED set to false, FALSE and invalid, and with a missing key file.

title: The emitted SSO handler takes its issuer and audience through the declared-value rule, which refuses another value

then: Expects the override refused with an error that names the variable; sso.go to take STEGO_AUTH_ISSUER and STEGO_AUTH_AUDIENCE through declaredValue and never through envOrDefault; and the handler to start.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestSSODeclaredTrustWins in the generated package that TestGeneratedSSOTrustPolicy builds and runs. Security review of PR #404, L4.

title: The emitted SSO handler refuses to start when AUTH_ENABLED is not empty or true
when: Starts the handler with no issuer, with no audience, with AUTH_ENABLED set to false, FALSE and invalid, and with a missing key file.

given: A service declaration with the jwt-auth and rh-sso-auth components, generated into a temporary folder.

notes: Level: unit. Not automated yet: no test names this ID yet. Candidate: TestGenerateSharedRuntime in internal/generator/rhssoauth/generator_test.go. Planned file internal/generator/rhssoauth/generator_test.go.

title: The service runs one key refresh task
given: A service declaration with the jwt-auth and rh-sso-auth components, generated into a temporary folder. A TLS JWKS test server counts requests.
