notes: Level: integration. Not automated yet: no test names this ID yet. Planned file internal/generator/rhssoauth/testdata/trust_test.go.

title: The emitted SSO handler refuses a nil or canceled startup context
when: Starts the handler with a nil context, then with a canceled context, then with a usable context.
then: Expects the nil and canceled contexts refused and the usable context accepted.

title: The emitted SSO handler leaves the process telemetry runtime open
when: Starts the handler with a nil runtime, a nil context, a usable pair, an invalid key document, a canceled context and an expired deadline, uses the runtime after the handler stops, then reads the local signal output.
then: Expects the invalid pairs refused, the runtime still usable after the handler closes, the five fixed outcomes in order, and no key path, key document or issuer in the output.

title: SSO startup telemetry from the emitted handler holds no private data
when: Starts the handler with a nil runtime, a nil context, a usable pair, an invalid key document, a canceled context and an expired deadline, uses the runtime after the handler stops, then reads the local signal output.
then: Expects the invalid pairs refused, the runtime still usable after the handler closes, the five fixed outcomes in order, and no key path, key document or issuer in the output.

title: A service with rh-sso-auth on the runtime data path gets the oidc-auth verifier with the Red Hat SSO settings
given: A rest-crud service declaration on the runtime data path with rh-sso-auth and its issuer and audience.
when: Generates the service with the tenancy claim tenant, then with org_id, and reads the emitted files; builds it and runs its migration job and its api mode with the issuer of a local test provider at https://127.0.0.1:<port>/auth/realms/redhat-external; sends an RS256 token with the Red Hat SSO claims sub, org_id, preferred_username and email, an ES256 token, a token with no org_id, a token of another issuer, an expired token, a token of an unknown key, a token for another audience, PS256 and alg none; reads an order of the first token with it and with tokens of another tenant and another subject; rotates the key after the cooldown; and starts the service with a discovery document of another issuer and with an http key set URL.
then: Expects the tenancy claim tenant refused with a fault that names org_id; the oidc-auth configuration with the Red Hat SSO issuer form, discovery, RS256 alone, the subject claim sub and the tenant claim org_id, and no verifier of rh-sso-auth's own; the RS256 token accepted after one discovery fetch and every other token refused with 401; the order seen by its owner only; the rotated key accepted with no second discovery fetch; and each bad start refused at the stage service.start.authn.discovery with no address in the failure record.
notes: Level: service. Proved by TestOIDCService: its subtests with this ID read the generated files and run the check testdata/oidc_test.go in the module of the generated service, whose subtest carries this ID. Local stand-ins (ST-STD-LOCAL): the key server of authn/authntest serves the discovery document and the key document of the issuer over TLS on 127.0.0.1 with its own certificate authority; PostgreSQL is the server of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN and SpiceDB a local serve container of the pinned image, without privilege. Mutations caught: the provider's tenant claim not checked against the tenancy claim, discovery not stated to the runtime, the stage of a refused start not named, ES256 taken, no tenant claim given (mut/mutate.py of b-oidc). The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11.

title: rh-sso-auth on the runtime data path takes the Red Hat SSO form and claims only
given: The settings of rh-sso-auth on the runtime data path with the issuer https://sso.redhat.com/auth/realms/redhat-external, an audience and a CA file.
when: Reads the settings, then with an issuer of another form, with a subpath, an http issuer, a key file, another key URL, other public paths and no audience.
then: Expects the issuer, the audience, the CA file, the subject claim sub, the tenant claim org_id and RS256 alone, and each of the other settings refused with a fault that names rh-sso-auth.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestRuntimeAuth; its subtest carries this ID. Mutations caught: the issuer form not checked, a key file taken, other public paths taken (mut/mutate.py of b-oidc).

title: The role migration makes the worker, relay, purge and outbox relay roles with the owner's SET memberships
given: A service declaration on the runtime data path with the tenancy, outbox and spicedb-authz components and one tenant-owned entity, and a fresh database in a local PostgreSQL.
when: Applies the role migration as the administrator, then runs the migration job with the login of the owner role, and reads pg_roles, pg_auth_members and has_schema_privilege.
then: Expects the roles <service>_worker and <service>_relay, and a migration job that passes with no role or grant made by hand. Also the purge role <service role prefix>_idempotency_purge and the outbox relay role <service role prefix>_outbox_relay, each with no login, no INHERIT, no BYPASSRLS, no superuser and no CREATE on public, the owner's membership in each WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE, and no runtime, worker or relay role a member of either.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest of this ID in the generated module's TestTenancy, which internal/generator/tenancy/generator_test.go (TestMigrations) runs and passes only when it passed: the role migration runs as the administrator and the migrations as the owner role; the test reads pg_roles, pg_auth_members and has_schema_privilege, and checks that no runtime, worker or relay role of the service is a member of the purge role or the outbox relay role. The migration job that passes with no role or grant made by hand is proved by ST-SUP-RP14-LC04-T02, whose check runs only the role migration and a login of each role before the job. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that the role migration makes these roles and grants. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): the PostgreSQL server is a local container without privilege (postgres:17.7), given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN; without it the test is skipped, and STEGO_REQUIRE_POSTGRES=1 makes that a failure. Mutation caught before ST-SUP-Q106: a role migration without the CREATE grant of the former cluster role on public. Security review of PR #206: the idempotency purge role. Recheck of PR #206 (F1): the purge role is the service's own; mutations caught: one purge role for the cluster, the owner inheriting it, a permanent CREATE on public for it (mut/round3.json of b-rt-harden). ST-SUP-Q106 (a): mutations caught: the owner inheriting the outbox relay role, a permanent CREATE on public for it, the role made with INHERIT (mut/round1.json of b-relay).

title: The outbox relay role is each service's own, and the owner of one service reaches no outbox of another
given: Two service declarations with the tenancy component and roles of their own, the outbox and authorization migrations of the runtime library, and a local PostgreSQL server.
when: Applies the role migration of the first service in its database. Makes the database of the second service, opens a session of the first service's owner in it and keeps it, and applies the second role migration; then, past its refusal, applies the rest of it, the outbox and authorization migrations as the second owner, and one message. From the held session, as itself and as its own outbox relay role, reads the second service's messages, runs its claim, purge and state hook functions, takes and grants its outbox relay role, takes its owner role, gives its claim function to another role and grants its messages. Then closes the session, applies the second role migration again, runs the migrations of each service twice as its owner, which is no superuser, and reads the messages of the first database as its owner.
then: Expects two outbox relay roles of different names, the role migration refused while the session is open, each attempt from the held session refused for privilege and the session still open, the first owner and its relay role no member of the second relay role, and the second message untouched. Expects the migrations to pass twice as each owner, the relay and state hook functions of each database owned by its own relay role, which keeps no CREATE on public or stego_outbox, and the first owner to see no message as itself and the message as its relay role, with SET ROLE.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest ST-SUP-RC27-OC04-T08 of TestRelayRoles in the generated module, which TestMigrations of internal/generator/tenancy runs; it passes the record only when that subtest passed there. The generated module requires the runtime library from the registry/runtime folder of this repository, whose outbox.Migration and authz.Migration it runs for the roles of each service. The server is the one that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names: a local postgres:17.7 container without privilege (ST-STD-LOCAL). ST-SUP-Q106 option (a), decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11). Mutations caught: one outbox relay role for the cluster, PUBLIC with EXECUTE on the relay functions, PUBLIC with EXECUTE on the state hook, the authorization migration keeping the CREATE it gave, no EXECUTE on the trigger function for the migration role (mut/round1.json of b-relay).

title: A role prefix whose role names can be another service's role names is refused
given: A service declaration with the tenancy component.
when: Validates and generates the service with the prefix shop_outbox, from the service name shop-outbox, from the runtime_role shop_outbox_runtime and from the runtime_role shop_outbox; then validates the prefixes outbox_shop, shop_outboxes, shop and outbox as <prefix>_runtime and <prefix>_owner. Then validates the settings runtime_role shop_outbox_relay, shop_worker and shop_owner, owner_role shop_outbox_relay and shop_owner, runtime_role x_runtime with owner_role shop_owner, runtime_role shop_runtime with owner_role app_owner, and runtime_role _runtime with owner_role _owner.
then: Expects each prefix shop_outbox refused by ValidateContext and Generate, with an error that names the role shop_outbox_relay and the other prefix shop, the other prefixes taken, and each of the settings refused as not <prefix>_runtime and <prefix>_owner of one prefix.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestGenerator. The check compares each pair of role suffixes (_runtime, _owner, _worker, _relay, _idempotency_purge, _outbox_relay): when one ends with the other, a prefix that ends with the rest is refused; today only _outbox. A configured owner_role is free text and is not compared across services. ST-SUP-Q107 option (a), decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-11. Mutations caught: no prefix check, _outbox_relay left out of the suffixes, a check that refuses any prefix that holds outbox, a check of the runtime role in place of its prefix (mut/round2.json of b-relay). Security review of PR #213 (F1, decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-11, in the security review of PR #213): the settings that named a role of another prefix; mutations caught: no suffix rule, no one-prefix rule (mut/round3.json of b-relay).

title: The role migration refuses a role of its names that is not this service's alone
given: A service declaration with the tenancy component, a local PostgreSQL server, a database of another service and a role of no service.
when: Makes, one at a time before the role migration, the owner role with a login and CONNECT on the other database, the outbox relay role with a login, and the runtime role as a member of the role of no service, and applies the role migration on a fresh database each time. Then drops them and applies the role migration on two fresh databases of the service, one after the other. Then a login with CREATEROLE that is no superuser makes the owner and runtime roles, and the role migration runs; then the runtime role, made again, is granted to a role of another service, and it runs; then the owner role is granted to a migration login, and it runs without and with stego.migration_login naming that login, and again after the login gets ADMIN.
then: Expects each run refused with an error that names the role and the sign, the role as it was, and PUBLIC still with CONNECT on the fresh database, so the text changed nothing. Expects both runs on the databases of the service to pass, since the owner holds CREATE on the first. Expects the roles that the CREATEROLE login made refused with that login named with ADMIN, the runtime role refused with the member of the other service named, the migration login refused while it is not named, taken when it is named, and refused when it holds ADMIN.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest ST-SUP-RC27-OC04-T10 of TestForeignRoles in the generated module, which TestMigrations of internal/generator/tenancy runs; it passes the record only when that subtest passed there. The server is the one that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names: a local postgres:17.7 container without privilege (ST-STD-LOCAL). Security review of PR #213 (F1, decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-11, in the security review of PR #213). The sign of another database leaves out a database on which the owner of this service holds CREATE, because the role migration of one service may run on more than one database of the cluster, as the runtime wiring check does with its foreign and legacy databases; two services of one prefix therefore stay one role set. Mutations caught: no sign of another database, no sign of a login, no sign of a membership, the sign of another database with no exception for a database of the service (mut/round3.json of b-relay). title: Create, update and delete each enqueue the declared tuples, and a change of a field subject is refused
given: The command generator's test declaration (serviceYAML in internal/generator/command/generator_test.go): the owned entity Hold with resource type hold, a reference order_id to Order with the relation order, the relationship creator from the caller (subject type user) and the relationship owner from the field owner_id (subject type user), and the command reserve-and-charge on order with the permission reserve, generated into a temp folder with its fill.
when: Creates a Hold with owner_id u1 as the caller u-7, updates it keeping owner_id u1, updates owner_id to u2, then deletes it, each in its own command.
then: Expects the update that keeps the owner to answer 201, the update that moves it to answer 400 with the code invalid and the field owner_id, and authz outbox entries for the Hold in this order: touch creator@user:<caller>, touch owner@user:u1; and the filtered deletes of the schema relations creator and owner of hold.
notes: Level: integration. internal/generator/command/service_test.go (TestCommandService) generates the service, builds it against the runtime module of this repository with the Go SDK of STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO, and runs this check of testdata/command_test.go there against the PostgreSQL server of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN and a local SpiceDB container of the pinned image authzed/spicedb:v1.57.0, without privilege (ST-STD-LOCAL). Each step is one command over HTTP whose fill uses the generated Hold repository, so the tuples come from the generated Relationships list through the command runtime, the path a service takes (ST-SUP-Q118). The test reads the authz outbox messages of the Hold, without the reference relation order, which ST-SUP-RP10-LC05-T12 proves. The test writes the creator tuple to SpiceDB itself, as the relay would, so the later commands may lock the Hold. The delete removes every tuple of each relation that the schema declares on hold by the filtered delete of the relation (ST-SUP-Q118, delete path 1 and M3); the test reads no message of the reference relation order. The subject of a field-sourced relationship is set at create only (ST-SUP-Q118). Mutations caught: no Relationships list emitted; no declared tuple written on create; an update that changes the field subject.

title: A grant lands through the relay and raises the floor, its revocation completes, and a check at the floor denies
given: A rest-crud service declaration with the spicedb-authz, durable-events and auth-provider components, the schema authz/schema.zed with the resource type document (relations owner and viewer; permissions view = owner + viewer and edit = owner), and the owned entity Document with resource type document, permissions read: view, list: view, create: edit, update: edit, delete: edit, and the relationship owner from the field owner_id with subject type user, generated into a temp folder.
when: Creates a Document owned by alice and lets the relay deliver; then moves the owner from alice to bob in one request and lets the relay deliver; then evaluates edit for alice and bob with consistency at least the token of the grant.
then: Expects the grant's revocation complete with the floor raised to the row's authz_token, alice allowed after the grant; the second revocation complete with the floor raised past the grant's token; and, at the grant's token, alice denied and bob allowed, because every check runs at least as fresh as the floor.
notes: Level: integration. The test builds the gen.Context of the declaration by hand, as the compiler gives it to the generator: pooled tenancy on tenant_id, the authorization setting and the schema authz/schema.zed among the inputs, and a second protected entity Project with the resource type project. internal/generator/spicedbauthz/generator_test.go (TestGeneratedAuthzWiring) generates the module into a temporary folder, builds it against the runtime module of this repository with the Go SDK of STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO, and runs this test there against the PostgreSQL server of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN and a local SpiceDB serve-testing container of the pinned image authzed/spicedb:v1.57.0, without privilege, which the test starts and removes (ST-STD-LOCAL). Each test makes a database of its own with a runtime role, an outbox worker role and a relay role, none a superuser, and applies the outbox runtime's migration, the tables documents, projects and notes with the tenant policy of the tenancy component, and the emitted Migration. The provider is the runtime's SpiceDB provider on a datastore of the test, to which the test writes the emitted Schema, as the deployment does. The evaluation goes through the Port of the emitted NewRuntime, which raises every check to the floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13). The status comes from the revocation record, which only the relay's state hook changes (ST-SUP-RP06-LC18), so a complete revocation also proves the hook that NewRelay registers.

title: A run again of the migration takes no lock on a protected table

then: Expects each read to return, and the run again to pass while the long transaction holds documents.

ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table even when the column is there, so the run again of a migration job would wait behind the long transaction of a running release, and every read and write of the table would queue behind it (followups.md P1, research F1). title: A ticker runs each tenant once a tick in its own transaction and skips an overlapping tick
given: The command runtime fixture of the worker tests on the local PostgreSQL server, the worker sync-partner-orders with the permission sync that writes orders, and a ticker of it on a fake clock that moves only when the test moves it.
when: Runs a ticker with a 10s interval over t1 and t2 and moves the clock to the first due time; then makes the fill block for t1, moves the clock to the next due time and once more while the fill blocks.

notes: Level: integration. The server is the one that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names: a local postgres:17.7 container without privilege (ST-STD-LOCAL). The service-level test T01 stays planned. Mutations caught (b-worker, 2026-11-14): a tick that runs while one runs. The helpers of the ticker fixture have no wall-clock guard and no sleep (rt121): the ticker gives each step of its scheduler (a wait armed for a due time, a skipped tick, the start and the end of a tick) to a hook of the tests, and each call of the fill comes to the fixture as it happens. next, waitArms and waitSkipped wait on these steps and fail when the ticker is at rest (no tick runs and the scheduler waits for a due time after the time now); none checks the calls after the step after which a call would have come; stopped moves the clock after Finish and expects Run to return with no tick. title: Of two instances only the lease holder runs a single worker
given: The module that the worker generator emits for the service of ST-SUP-RC35-OC01-T01 (the workers sync-partner-orders, every 1m and single, and apply-partner-replies), with the domain-probe output and the fill sync-orders, whose behavior the check sets, built on the runtime library of this repository. The check package runs the generated runners.Tickers with runners.BoundFills on a service.TickerEnv as the worker mode builds it: the command runtime of the workers on one local PostgreSQL database with the tenant list, the entity tables and the lease row stego.worker.sync-partner-orders, a decision port that allows each request, a probe recorder of the built-in worker observations for each instance, and a test clock that moves only when the check moves it. Each check adds its own tenants, each with one order, and retires them at its end. In OC05 each instance ticks on a test clock of its own, and the lease clients of both instances use one more test clock, the lease clock, with a lease TTL of one hour, a renew of 2 s and a retry of 1 s: only the check moves the lease clock, so no renew, retry or expiry happens between two steps of the check.
when: Starts the instance h1 and waits until it waits for the due time, then starts h2 and waits until it waits for its retry of the lease; moves both tick clocks to the due time. Then gives the lease row to h2, waits until h1 waits for its renew and moves the lease clock by the renew, so the renew of h1 fails and h2 takes the lease at its retry; waits until h1 waits to take the lease again and h2 waits for the next due time, and moves both tick clocks to it.
then: Expects the lease row held by h1 while h1 waits for a tick; h2 waiting for the lease and never for a tick; one fill call at the first due time, whose run commits, and no other call; after the renew of h1 failed, the lease row held by h2, one fill call at the next due time, whose run commits, and no other call. Before each check of no other call, the check proves that no party can call the fill: the run committed, and each other instance waits for the lease clock, which the check does not move (h2 never waited on its tick clock; h1 waits for its retry of the lease).
notes: Level: service. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestWorker in the check package of the generated module, which TestService of internal/generator/worker runs with go test; it passes the record only when that subtest passed there. The check does not depend on time: each step waits for the wait of the clock that the next step needs, with no deadline, and only the timeout of go test bounds it (CI flake of 2026-11-15, fixed by rt117). The wait for the first of two clock waits gives each wait that is there, so the check of h2 is exact (security review of PR #376, L4). The server is the one that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names: a local postgres:17.7 container without privilege (ST-STD-LOCAL). Mutations caught (b-worker, 2026-11-14; rt117, 2026-11-16): a single worker that ticks without its lease.

when: Waits until the relay delivered every message for authz and reads the tuples of the tenant resource of each other active tenant; adds a tenant whose ID sorts after the others to the tenant list with no tuple of the declared workers and writes the tuple tenant:<tenant resource>#worker_retired_export@service_account:retired-export to SpiceDB, as after a release that added and removed workers; stops the service and starts it again, as a rollout does, so the controller mode runs the job worker-tuples at start; reads the tuples of that tenant resource from SpiceDB, fully consistent, until they match; reads the audit rows, the tuple writes and the tuples of the other tenants, and the readiness of the modes.
then: Expects SpiceDB to hold the tuples of worker_apply_note_replies and worker_sync_partner_orders of their own service accounts on that tenant resource and no tuple of worker_retired_export; one audit row reconcile-worker-tuples of the actor kind system in the tenant's own chain with the tenant as the resource; no tuple write for another tenant since the restart and the tuples of each other tenant as before; and the readiness of the modes 200, and never a readiness that names worker-tuples.
notes: Level: service. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestWiring in the module of the generated service of testdata/runtime_wiring, which TestRuntimeWiring of internal/compiler runs; it passes the record only when that subtest passed there. The service runs against a local postgres:17.7 container and a local SpiceDB v1.57.0 container without privilege (ST-STD-LOCAL). The wait for SpiceDB has no deadline of its own. Each wait logs the state that it saw last each 10 s, so a wait that never ends can be read in the log (security review of PR #379).

title: Only a binary of the release identity row reconciles or deletes undeclared worker tuples, and Retire always deletes its declared workers' tuples
given: The fixture of ST-SUP-RC35-OC13-T05 with the active tenants org-a, org-b and org-c, where SpiceDB holds the tuple of worker_old_sync on org-a, the reconcile of the release step_0002_add-x_expand with the workers sync-partner-orders and apply-partner-replies, and ServeTenant for Provision and Retire with the same workers, the fake reader of SpiceDB and the same release.
when: Runs the reconcile with no release identity row, with the row of another release and with the row of another worker set; then with its own row and a reader that writes the row of another worker set when it first reads; then retires org-a with no row, org-b with the row of another release and org-c with its own row.
then: Expects the workers digest of the two workers to be da200a1d8cb9d7dea09dde2570b5341b474a1c3c234361ea5e13598d40e8a7d1 in any order, the vector of ST-SUP-RC35-OC13-T09; each fenced run to visit no tenant, write no outbox message and no audit row, report itself fenced, and log one notice command.worker_tuples.fenced with the job, its own identity and the identity of the row (missing for no row) only; the run whose row changes to write nothing; and each Retire to stage the deletes of the two declared workers' tuples, and only the Retire of org-c, with its own row, the delete of the relation worker_old_sync too. Each notice is a warning; the job is not degraded after 0, 1 or 2 fenced runs and is degraded after 3 in a row with the reason fenced: identity row <row identity> is not <own identity>; a run with its own row and nothing to change is not fenced and ends the degraded state.
notes: Level: integration. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege, given to the test as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN; the reader of SpiceDB is a fake. Security review of PR #379, M2 and L1. Mutations caught (rt118, 2026-11-16): the declared deletes of Retire fenced; no fence at the start of the run; no fence in the transaction of a tenant; the undeclared deletes of Retire not fenced; an identity that compares the release only. Security re-review of PR #379, L-b. Mutations caught: never degraded; degraded after one run; no reset after a run that is not fenced.

title: Retire and the reconcile take their locks in one order, and the reconcile stops when it loses the lease
given: The fixture of ST-SUP-RC35-OC13-T07 with the active tenants org-a and org-b, which hold no worker tuple, and ServeTenant for Retire.
when: Runs the reconcile, which stops in the transaction of org-a after it took the lock of the worker tuples of org-a; sends the Retire of org-a through ServeTenant; waits until a session waits for an advisory lock, and lets the reconcile go on; then runs the reconcile with a lease whose fence fails.
then: Expects the Retire to wait for the lock and answer 200, the reconcile to end with no error and no deadlock, and org-a to hold the two touches of the reconcile, then the two deletes and the delete of the relation worker_old_sync of the Retire; and the run with the lost lease to visit one tenant, change none, fail with an error of the class lease and write nothing.
notes: Level: integration. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 in a local container without privilege. The waits have no deadline and log the state they see each 2 s. Security review of PR #379, M1 and L3: the lock of the worker tuples is the first lock of a Provision or Retire, before the key of the request and the chain lock of the audit row (ST-SUP-RP10-LC06). Mutations caught (rt118, 2026-11-16): the lock taken after the audit row (a deadlock, and the Retire answers 500); no fence of the lease.

when: Computes the workers digest of the two names in both orders and of no name, the note of the release identity, and the plan text with that note; then the note of the same service with no provisioning.
then: Expects da200a1d8cb9d7dea09dde2570b5341b474a1c3c234361ea5e13598d40e8a7d1 in both orders and the SHA-256 of the empty text for no name; a note that holds the digest and the sorted workers; the plan text with the line note: and the note; and no note with no provisioning.
notes: Level: unit. The same vector holds tenant.WorkersDigest of the runtime in ST-SUP-RC35-OC13-T07, so the plan shows the digest that the migration job writes.

title: With no definition tenant, or a failed read of the schema, Retire still retires and deletes its declared workers' tuples, and the reconcile writes nothing
given: The fixture of ST-SUP-RC35-OC13-T07 with the active tenants org-a, org-b and org-c; a fake reader of SpiceDB whose read of the schema gives authz.ErrNoDefinition, as for the schema of examples/user-management; and a fake reader whose read of the schema fails for another cause.
when: Retires org-a through ServeTenant with no worker and the first reader, and runs the reconcile with no worker and that reader; then retires org-b with the two workers and the second reader.
then: Expects the retire of org-a to answer 200; the reconcile to end with no error, not fenced, and with no write, so the job stays healthy; the retire of org-b to answer 200, retire it and stage only the deletes of its two declared workers' tuples; one warn line command.worker_tuples.read_failed with the command and the class schema_read only; and no log line that names a tenant.

Mutations caught (rt118, 2026-11-16): a Retire that fails on a failed read; a Retire or a reconcile that takes ErrNoDefinition as a failure.

title: The generated user-management example provisions a tenant, creates and reads an organization, retires the tenant, and stays ready
given: A copy of examples/user-management as the repository holds it, with its generated service built against the runtime module of this repository: pooled tenancy with provisioning on service:user-management, the event-publisher mixin, no declared worker, and a schema with no definition tenant. A new database on the local PostgreSQL server with the role migration of the example and a login of each role, the migration job run as the owner role, a local SpiceDB container and the local Kafka broker of kafkatest. The service runs in all modes and reaches SpiceDB through a proxy that counts its calls by method.
when: Waits until /readyz and /readyz/modes answer 200 and a controller holds the controller lease; provisions a tenant as an operator who holds operator on service:user-management; creates one organization as a user of that tenant, writes the owner relation of the user on it, and reads it; retires the tenant; then stops the service and starts it again, and waits until the new controller holds the lease.
then: Expects the provision to answer 201, the create 201, the read 200 with the id and the name of the create and at least one CheckPermission call through the proxy, the retire 200 with a retire time in the tenant list, and a read in the retired tenant 403 with the code tenant.not_provisioned (ST-SUP-RC27-OC11); /readyz and /readyz/modes to answer 200 with one line that names no job after the start, after the read, after the retire and after the new start; and no call of ReflectSchema by the service, since a schema with no definition tenant gives no worker-tuples job and no read of worker relations at Retire.
notes: Level: system. Proved by the subtest of the same ID of TestProvisionRetire in the module of a copy of examples/user-management, which TestRuntimeExample of internal/compiler runs with testdata/runtime_example/check/example_test.go after the checks of that file; it passes the record only when that subtest passed there (follow-up of the #379 gap: the other checks of the example add their tenants as the administrator, and nothing ran Provision and Retire of a generated example against PostgreSQL and SpiceDB). Local stand-ins (ST-STD-LOCAL): the PostgreSQL server of STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, and the SpiceDB container and the kafkatest broker of the runtime example test, each without privilege. The checks of the example run one after the other in one test binary, as they share the server roles of the example. The waits have no deadline of their own; only the timeout of go test bounds them. The unit proof of Retire and the reconcile with no definition tenant is ST-SUP-RC35-OC13-T10.

then: Expects the contract to hold SyncPartnerOrdersUnsynced, a command.List of Order with the Read and Lock statements over the column list of the entity's Scan, the tenant as $1, the filter as $3 and $4, ORDER BY the key and, for Lock, the key array and FOR NO KEY UPDATE, with the Values false and done; the entity to hold LockAtMost 10; the runners to give it in the WorkerSpec of sync-partner-orders only; the release with the new fields to give its columns, the time of the run and int64(3), and no Lock; and each of the last four refused with an error that names the worker and the list or the Lock at most.

title: A consumer whose worker tuple is missing parks nothing and runs the message after the tuple is written
given: The fixture of ST-SUP-RC35-OC06-T05: the consumer apply-partner-replies on a local PostgreSQL database with the held clock, and a reader of SpiceDB that answers that the tuple of the worker is missing.

title: A destination is registered with the delivery that it declares, and an idempotent one needs a partner that accepts the key
given: A service declaration with the modes api and worker, the durable-events mixin and the https-destination component with the destination partner-orders (origin https://partner.test, path /v1/orders, method POST, must_land true, idempotent true, the partner accepts an Idempotency-Key, status path /v1/orders/status, settle 5s, timeout 2s, credential partner-token), the worker sync-partner-orders (every 10s, writes Order, effect partner-orders: order-changed) bound to its fill, generated into a temp folder, built and started in process on a local PostgreSQL with the emitted fake partner as the origin and its test CA as the only trust root.
when: Generates and starts the service and reads the outbox's destination registry; then does the same with idempotent false and stages one effect, and makes the fake partner accept the request and drop the connection before it answers; then checks the declaration with idempotent true and a partner that does not accept an Idempotency-Key.
then: Expects partner-orders registered once and as idempotent; then registered as not idempotent, the message in reconciling and not sent again; and the last declaration refused at checking with a fault that names partner-orders.
notes: Level: service. Not automated yet: the generator package internal/generator/httpsdestination does not exist yet. Planned file internal/compiler/testdata/https_destination_test.go. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): the partner is the in-process fake partner of ST-SUP-RC36-OC08 over TLS with a test CA, so the test reaches no network; the PostgreSQL server runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it. Decision on ST-SUP-Q41 (2026-11-07, under the Product owner's delegation): the registry offers an outbound HTTPS destination component for partner calls, so a worker or a command reaches a partner's HTTPS API only through the outbox. Decision of 2026-11-07 on the review of PR 125, under the Product owner's delegation: not acted needs a positive answer that echoes the key, the key goes in the Idempotency-Key header, 409 is transient for an idempotent destination, the body is the effect as JSON, and the credential is read again on each request. The orchestrator decided under the owner's delegation (2026-11-11) that the declaration states idempotent for every destination and the component refuses an idempotent destination whose partner does not accept the key, and no longer derives the property (ST-SUP-RC32-OC12).

title: Only an answer that echoes the key reconciles an unknown outcome
given: A service declaration with the modes api and worker, the durable-events mixin and the https-destination component with the destination partner-orders (origin https://partner.test, path /v1/orders, method POST, idempotent no, status path /v1/orders/status, settle 5s, timeout 2s, credential partner-token), the worker sync-partner-orders (every 10s, writes Order, effect partner-orders: order-changed) bound to its fill, generated into a temp folder, built and started in process on a local PostgreSQL with the emitted fake partner as the origin and its test CA as the only trust root.
when: Stages one effect, makes the fake partner act on the request and drop the connection, and answers the lookup with 200 and {"idempotency_key": key, "state": "acted"}; repeats with a partner that did not act and answers not_acted with the key; then with 404; then with not_acted and another key; then with 500 to every lookup.
then: Expects each lookup sent after the deadline plus 5s with the header Idempotency-Key of the message; the first message done; the second pending and then delivered once; the third, the fourth and the fifth kept in reconciling as unknown and parked when their lookups are exhausted.
notes: Level: service. Not automated yet: the generator package internal/generator/httpsdestination does not exist yet. Planned file internal/compiler/testdata/https_destination_test.go. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): the partner is the in-process fake partner of ST-SUP-RC36-OC08 over TLS with a test CA, so the test reaches no network; the PostgreSQL server runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it. Decision on ST-SUP-Q41 (2026-11-07, under the Product owner's delegation): the registry offers an outbound HTTPS destination component for partner calls, so a worker or a command reaches a partner's HTTPS API only through the outbox. Decision of 2026-11-07 on the review of PR 125, under the Product owner's delegation: not acted needs a positive answer that echoes the key, the key goes in the Idempotency-Key header, 409 is transient for an idempotent destination, the body is the effect as JSON, and the credential is read again on each request.

title: A plain HTTP origin is refused, and an unverified partner gets no request
